chapters.title: Chapter 771: Reaching the 5th Level
paragraphs: After attaining weak flame comprehension, Kent increased his pace, hoping to reach the 5th level and master all techniques before the day was over.

He was moving steadily, and the progress was evident in the fact that, while he was nowhere close to attaining High Flame Resistance, he was also sure that jumping into a sea of flames wouldn’t be impossible.
His body has grown rather stubborn to heat and flames.
Meanwhile, at the 2nd level, the seven survivalists finally arrived.
It wasn’t a struggle for them to climb to the 2nd level, so they got there as quickly as they could.
"Kent said we should learn one Enhancement Flame Art, one Attacking Flame Art, and two Defense Flame Arts," Lorin said, looking at the variety of friends she had just made.
They nodded at her words, already knowing that their mission was almost in the bag.
"Let’s get it done within five hours so we can move to the 3rd level." With that resolve, they started looking for the flame arts they would be learning.
This time, Kent wouldn’t be selecting for them, so they had to do that themselves, though Kent was sure they would get what would benefit them in the long run.
In the world of cultivation, many believe that having the strongest attack skill would make up for the lack of defense. However, while that may be true, it only applies to swordsmen most of the time.
Swordsmen primarily focus on their sword skills and techniques that allow them to unleash lethal attacks, so they mostly just use their attacks to defend.
However, those lacking both offense and defense are bound to get crushed regardless of what one thinks.
Kent saw this and knew that, while the seven he had selected may seem like geniuses to those outside, the truth of the matter was that they weren’t. They can’t be counted among the geniuses.
However, they have something geniuses don’t think is needed, the ability to adapt. They can adapt, and that is the quality that makes them dangerous.
In battle, if your opponent manages to adapt to your combat style, skills, and techniques, the chances of you losing become high.
And that is how the survivalists fight. They adapt, and to do that, they need stronger defenses. They aren’t the brightest swordsmen who can use offense as defense.
So, he made it clear that learning more defensive techniques would work magic in the long run.
If they manage to master the Flame Art for defense, they will be able to save their skins and survive long enough to kill their opponents.
They got to work. They have 4 Flame Arts to learn.
Meanwhile, on the steps leading to the 4th level, Kella, the Elf lady, had started climbing again, already moving closer to the 60th step.
Kent helped her realize her misplaced determination.
In the quest to be like the daughters and sons of the Elven Lords, she had lost sight of how amazing she really was.

She was born a genius, and that alone was reason enough for her to be okay with what she had. But reality made her believe that being as amazing as the royalty or having the best clothes to wear and a big mansion to live in was all there was.
She had been blindly chasing after something she could build for herself.
She forgot that if she one day made it into the sect and managed to make a name for herself there, the life she had always wanted would become hers.
Standing at the peak would mean she and her father would have a good life, the kind she had been looking for all these years.
She was blinded, but Kent had finally opened her eyes to the truth, and now, she wanted nothing more than to climb the stairs and create the life she wanted for herself and her father.
She wouldn’t chase after people who had it good from the start. She wouldn’t chase after the royalty who could get anything they wanted with a wave of their hand.

She wanted none of that, for she now wanted to create a life where she stood above all of them. She wanted to surpass them all, and with that determination and resolve, she was moving steadily, heading slowly to the 4th level.
Kent’s friends were still absorbing the essence of the pill they’d taken. Of course, they were moving closer to awakening an Innate Talent.
Kent didn’t know what talent they would be awakening, but he knew that since they took it while under the heat of the flame tower, their innate talents would be flame-related.
Of course, he expected something like that to happen, so he wanted them to enter the tower first before taking the pills.

If they truly managed to awaken a flame-related innate talent, then this year’s batch of half-elves would dominate the entire world, for they would become some of the most dangerous cultivators in the world.
This would also mean Kent would be getting much more soul essence. Ultimately, it was all about the soul’s essence.
Kent, on the other hand, was moving closer to the 5th level. He had already climbed to the 95th step and was moving closer to the 100th.
"I wonder what will become of me after mastering divine-grade techniques. I am sure everyone will freak out, but who could blame them?
They haven’t met someone as awesome as me. If they had, they would’ve known I am no simple person."
With the bragging rights in his hand, Kent kept moving closer to the 5th level. Slowly but surely, he managed to reach the 5th level.
The moment he stepped on the last step to the 5th level, just like with the other levels, he felt his surroundings calm down, and the heat in the air vanished.
Kent appeared in a large hall where 12 tomes hovered in the air, each housing a divine-grade flame art. Kent moved toward them and started looking at their names.
It took him just a few glances to know he had indeed stepped into the pool of powerful flame arts.
"There are four Enhancement Flame Arts, five Attacking Flame Arts, and three Defensive Flame Arts."
Kent, note down the name of the techniques and choose to learn an enhancement-type technique.
Within five minutes, he learned all five forms of the technique.
"Well, that is just too great. With a tap, I was able to learn such a powerful divine grade flame art." Kent activated the first form of the ’Firestep Divine Dance,’ and his legs ignited into flames.
Instantly, Kent felt his speed soar, giving him the means to move twice as fast as before. But that was just the first form, ’Flame Foot.’
Kent quickly activated the second form, and the flame around his legs turned into combat boots, increasing his speed to three times his original speed.
"Holy smokes... Just this alone is enough to dance between attacks." Kent laughed, feeling the rush of speed. He then activated the third form, and the shoes grew flame wings.
"Damn, when moving through the air, my speed increases by four times. That is enough to make me nearly invisible to the naked eye."
The fourth form of the skill turns the winged shoes into jet shoes. A thruster appeared beneath the shoe, pushing Kent’s speed to eight times his original speed.

Then came the ultimate form, which turns the shoes into two rings on both the left and right legs. At that very moment, Kent felt like he could move at a speed that would be nearly impossible to track.
"Damn... this is good."

sentences.text: After attaining weak flame comprehension, Kent increased his pace, hoping to reach the 5th level and master all techniques before the day was over.

He was moving steadily, and the progress was evident in the fact that, while he was nowhere close to attaining High Flame Resistance, he was also sure that jumping into a sea of flames wouldn’t be impossible.
His body has grown rather stubborn to heat and flames.
Meanwhile, at the 2nd level, the seven survivalists finally arrived.
It wasn’t a struggle for them to climb to the 2nd level, so they got there as quickly as they could.
"Kent said we should learn one Enhancement Flame Art, one Attacking Flame Art, and two Defense Flame Arts," Lorin said, looking at the variety of friends she had just made.
They nodded at her words, already knowing that their mission was almost in the bag.
"Let’s get it done within five hours so we can move to the 3rd level." With that resolve, they started looking for the flame arts they would be learning.
This time, Kent wouldn’t be selecting for them, so they had to do that themselves, though Kent was sure they would get what would benefit them in the long run.
In the world of cultivation, many believe that having the strongest attack skill would make up for the lack of defense.
However, while that may be true, it only applies to swordsmen most of the time.
Swordsmen primarily focus on their sword skills and techniques that allow them to unleash lethal attacks, so they mostly just use their attacks to defend.
However, those lacking both offense and defense are bound to get crushed regardless of what one thinks.
Kent saw this and knew that, while the seven he had selected may seem like geniuses to those outside, the truth of the matter was that they weren’t.
They can’t be counted among the geniuses.
However, they have something geniuses don’t think is needed, the ability to adapt.
They can adapt, and that is the quality that makes them dangerous.
In battle, if your opponent manages to adapt to your combat style, skills, and techniques, the chances of you losing become high.
And that is how the survivalists fight.
They adapt, and to do that, they need stronger defenses.
They aren’t the brightest swordsmen who can use offense as defense.
So, he made it clear that learning more defensive techniques would work magic in the long run.
If they manage to master the Flame Art for defense, they will be able to save their skins and survive long enough to kill their opponents.
They got to work.
They have 4 Flame Arts to learn.
Meanwhile, on the steps leading to the 4th level, Kella, the Elf lady, had started climbing again, already moving closer to the 60th step.
Kent helped her realize her misplaced determination.
In the quest to be like the daughters and sons of the Elven Lords, she had lost sight of how amazing she really was.
She was born a genius, and that alone was reason enough for her to be okay with what she had.
But reality made her believe that being as amazing as the royalty or having the best clothes to wear and a big mansion to live in was all there was.
She had been blindly chasing after something she could build for herself.
She forgot that if she one day made it into the sect and managed to make a name for herself there, the life she had always wanted would become hers.
Standing at the peak would mean she and her father would have a good life, the kind she had been looking for all these years.
She was blinded, but Kent had finally opened her eyes to the truth, and now, she wanted nothing more than to climb the stairs and create the life she wanted for herself and her father.
She wouldn’t chase after people who had it good from the start.
She wouldn’t chase after the royalty who could get anything they wanted with a wave of their hand.
She wanted none of that, for she now wanted to create a life where she stood above all of them.
She wanted to surpass them all, and with that determination and resolve, she was moving steadily, heading slowly to the 4th level.
Kent’s friends were still absorbing the essence of the pill they’d taken.
Of course, they were moving closer to awakening an Innate Talent.
Kent didn’t know what talent they would be awakening, but he knew that since they took it while under the heat of the flame tower, their innate talents would be flame-related.
Of course, he expected something like that to happen, so he wanted them to enter the tower first before taking the pills.

If they truly managed to awaken a flame-related innate talent, then this year’s batch of half-elves would dominate the entire world, for they would become some of the most dangerous cultivators in the world.
This would also mean Kent would be getting much more soul essence.
Ultimately, it was all about the soul’s essence.
Kent, on the other hand, was moving closer to the 5th level.
He had already climbed to the 95th step and was moving closer to the 100th.
"I wonder what will become of me after mastering divine-grade techniques.
I am sure everyone will freak out, but who could blame them?
They haven’t met someone as awesome as me.
If they had, they would’ve known I am no simple person."
With the bragging rights in his hand, Kent kept moving closer to the 5th level.
Slowly but surely, he managed to reach the 5th level.
The moment he stepped on the last step to the 5th level, just like with the other levels, he felt his surroundings calm down, and the heat in the air vanished.
Kent appeared in a large hall where 12 tomes hovered in the air, each housing a divine-grade flame art.
Kent moved toward them and started looking at their names.
It took him just a few glances to know he had indeed stepped into the pool of powerful flame arts.
"There are four Enhancement Flame Arts, five Attacking Flame Arts, and three Defensive Flame Arts."
Kent, note down the name of the techniques and choose to learn an enhancement-type technique.
Within five minutes, he learned all five forms of the technique.
"Well, that is just too great.
With a tap, I was able to learn such a powerful divine grade flame art." Kent activated the first form of the ’Firestep Divine Dance,’ and his legs ignited into flames.
Instantly, Kent felt his speed soar, giving him the means to move twice as fast as before.
But that was just the first form, ’Flame Foot.’
Kent quickly activated the second form, and the flame around his legs turned into combat boots, increasing his speed to three times his original speed.
"Holy smokes...
Just this alone is enough to dance between attacks." Kent laughed, feeling the rush of speed.
He then activated the third form, and the shoes grew flame wings.
"Damn, when moving through the air, my speed increases by four times.
That is enough to make me nearly invisible to the naked eye."
The fourth form of the skill turns the winged shoes into jet shoes.
A thruster appeared beneath the shoe, pushing Kent’s speed to eight times his original speed.
Then came the ultimate form, which turns the shoes into two rings on both the left and right legs.
At that very moment, Kent felt like he could move at a speed that would be nearly impossible to track.
"Damn... this is good."

chapters.title: Chapter 772: Impossible [Bonus]
paragraphs: "Impossible."
Elder Lance almost shouted, looking at the display board. The two disciples behind him stood with their eyes wide open, staring at the display board like two idiots.
The various leaders from the different races also stood there, looking at the display board, unsure of what to say.
The names displayed on the board were just too much for them to handle at the moment.
>>> FLAME TOWER PARTICIPANT RANKING CHART<<<
1. Kent Madson - Flame Art (10) - Grade (Divine) - Mastered Forms (complete mastery) - Level (5)
2. Freya Stoneforge - Flame Art (2) - Grade (Mythic) - Mastered Forms (3/7) - Level (4)
The scoreboard changed again, and this time, everybody started to wonder just what the hell was going on.
Kent’s name was seated at the top, having mastered ten divine flame arts. Ten fucking divine-grade flame arts, and that was just too much for any of them to handle.
"How is this possible? How can one learn ten divine-grade techniques in less than an hour?" Elder Lance wondered, already sweating.
He came to the world of Sonox with little to no expectations, but at the moment, he could feel his blood boiling, not out of rage but shock.
Remove Kent from the equation and focus on the second-ranked player down to the fifteenth.
Freya Stoneforge had already learned two mythic-grade flame arts. The last time this happened was when the Pill Princess reached the 4th level and learned two mythic-grade techniques.
However, even back then, it took her almost two days to learn, and she nearly failed to learn the second technique.
Not only had someone managed to reach the 4th level much faster, but she had also mastered two mythic-grade flame arts. That was just too much for anyone to comprehend.
Back to Kent.
He had already proven to everyone what kind of monster he was, and the look on everyone’s face showed shock.
The Flame Dragon King looked at his elders. "How come we never knew of such a talent?"

"That was because until recently, he was on the human continent, and apparently, he was being hunted down by the Hand. He came to Elarion and chose to side with the Half-Elves. However, I never expected him to be this impressive."
King Veyron looked at the Half-Elves and saw the smug expressions on their faces. Kent had told them he would attribute everything to them so they would benefit from his brilliance.
This meant the status of the Half-Elves would rise soon, and it would be thanks to Kent, who had now joined them.
’Lucky bastards,’ King Veyron cursed at the Half-Elves.

Of course, that was all he could do. However, knowing there was this kind of genius among the Half-Elves, he knew something had to be done quickly, lest the dragons lose their dominance in the world of Sonox.
He looked toward the Crystal Dragon King, and the king nodded.
That small gesture contained some serious messages that one could comprehend. It would make anyone turn pale if they knew.
King Veyron looked at the Earth Dragon King and received the same nod.
Meanwhile, Queen Elenara wasn’t sure if it was her eyes or if Kent had just mastered ten divine-grade flame arts.
"Just how is any of this possible?" she muttered, looking dazed.
Usually, in events like this, the Elves turned to dominate.
But this time around, not only had a human managed to learn ten divine-grade flame arts, but even the second through the fifteenth spots were occupied by people she had initially looked down on.
That was both humiliating and borderline infuriating.
But the results were clear on the display board, and there was nothing she could do about it.
’This kid must die, else these half-breeds will grow a pair, and I can’t allow that to happen.’ Her delusion still prevented her from seeing reason, and that alone was why she would doom her race.

Meanwhile, the demons were riding a different wave. The display listed the names of some of their people, but the fact that Kent had managed to learn ten divine-grade flame arts told them all they needed to know.
"We need to get him on our side, and to do that, we need to get in the good graces of the Half-Elves," King Draxon, the Incubus King, said, looking at the display board.

"We should do that right when we leave here. I believe with this kid’s potential, we can finally gain the advantage our race needs," Queen Seraphina, the Succubus Queen, seconded what the Incubus King said.
The other demon kings and queens nodded to her words. So far, they were the only races with no active ways to explore the world outside their own.
A few had managed to reach the High World using the tribulation method, but that was much more perilous, as it resulted in the loss of many geniuses.
So they knew that getting to know Kent now meant that if he were to gain strength one day, he could help them acquire at least one ascension platform.
They were hopeful and knew things would work out as long as they stayed on Kent’s good side.
As for the dwarves, they were pleased to see their princess had already mastered two mythic-grade techniques.
They never expected her to master two mythic-grade techniques that fast, but they were aware she intended to climb to the 4th level, for she had trained for it.
Now, seeing her succeed was all they could have asked for. They were happy, especially her father, who couldn’t stop smiling.
The beasts were also hopeful that their people would be able to make them proud. Some had already shown promising results, and that was all they could ask for.
Their true geniuses had already received invites from the sect and would be taking the exams in a week, so seeing more join the roster was already enough for them.
More names were added, and by the time the day ended, the arrangement started to shift even more.
Elder Lance was quiet the entire time, for he didn’t understand how any of this was possible. He had seen geniuses in the sect, but this was his first time seeing something this bizarre.
"Elder Lance, what should we do?" the male disciple behind him asked, already knowing what kind of chaos this would cause in the sect when news broke out.
"We can watch now and report everything to the supreme elders later. I am sure they will know what to do. Until then, not a word to anyone when we go back."

chapters.title: Chapter 773: Flame Innate Body
paragraphs: "That is the last of them," Kent said, stepping away from the last Flame Art he had just learned. There were twelve flame arts in total, and he learned them all
"These skills will take me a long way if I want to use my flame in combat." Kent smiled. Though his focus was on the sword, having powerful techniques like this wasn’t bad.
He had already seen what Chaos could do with his fist, and that was why he also wanted to have more than one profession.
Of course, his love for the sword would never fade, but if he was going to benefit from the life he had led, then he must master other aspects of himself.
So far, when it comes to the brawler class, thanks to Chaos, he could fight with his fists and claws. Of course, there was the part where he was also an assassin, thanks to the Faceless Assassin.
Though he had yet to know more of that life, some basic dagger skills wouldn’t escape his fingertips.
He can handle his dagger in ways somebody like him, who doesn’t have an assassin class, shouldn’t be able to do.
Basically, he already had some form of mastery over those parts of him, and now, he could move further with flame arts.
He had already attained some form of comprehension of flames, meaning he now had to build his understanding of the flame and learn how to control it.
It may sound like a lot of work, but in the grand scheme of things, he would see the benefit.
His sword mastery was already on another level, and now with his comprehension of the flame unlocked, he was already looking for a future where his control over the flame would become unrivaled.
He can even go further and merge the flame arts with his sword, adding a new aspect to his already robust sword path.
"Now that I have done what I came here to do, I don’t have anything else to do but wait for the time to reach." Kent sat down, fell back, and closed his eyes.
Within seconds, he drifted into sleep without a care for anything. He had nothing to do again, so he might as well relax.
He knew when it was time to leave, the tower would alert him, so he relaxed and started to wait for the time to end.
However, three minutes into his nap, something changed. From one side of the wall, a flame symbol flew slowly as if it wanted to sneak up on Kent.
It moved slowly, and when it reached Kent’s side, it hovered for a few seconds and entered his forehead.
Kent, who didn’t know what had happened, remained asleep, unaware of the flame tattoos appearing all over his body, as if he were being examined by something profound.
Ten hours had passed since the Flame Tower opened, and everyone with a flame token had entered with big dreams.
Some entered in hopes of bringing glory to their race.
Others entered to make a name for themselves.
While the rest wanted to carve a path for themselves, since that was the only path they could walk.
Getting into the Supreme Immortal Sect was their ultimate goal.
However, the universe can be cruel sometimes. While these youngsters dreamed and hoped for the best, only a few would realize their dreams.
There were people still struggling at the first level, and many were still thinking they could make it to the second level.
Those who had started to contemplate whether they should return to the first level and try their hands at the heaven-grade techniques were also battling their inner thoughts.
Though their chances of passing the Sect entrance exams were slim, they could take the chance and hope for the best.
However, while most were struggling, others were making shocking progress.
The seven survivalists managed to learn all four Flame Arts they picked.
They had given themselves five hours to learn all four, but they managed to complete it in three and a half hours, leaving them with more time to progress to the third level.
They weren’t like Kent, whose soul was enormous. All of them were Tier 10 in soul cultivation, so they couldn’t learn all the techniques like Kent could.
So instead of getting greedy, they paid attention to all the instructions and warnings Kent had given them before leaving.
This was why, after learning the four legendary-grade techniques, they left and started climbing to the third level.
Meanwhile, Kella was currently standing on the 98th step, just two steps away from reaching her goal. It was in sight, but it would probably take her an hour to make the last two steps.
A couple of steps behind her were the eight half-elves still in lotus posture. They had been seated on the steps for hours now, and so everyone who passed by wondered just what they were up to.
However, while they would have loved to know, they also couldn’t wait to learn what they were up to. Time was of the essence, so they left to handle their jobs.
However, if they had waited, at precisely fifteen hours after the tower awakened, they would have seen perhaps the most beautiful thing.
Kella was fortunate to have witnessed Princess Elowen’s innate talent awaken, and while her side and the half-elves didn’t see eye to eye, she was mesmerized by what she saw.
At exactly fifteen hours after the opening, Princess Elowen’s eyes and hair lit up with white, freezing cold flame—the kind that made the temperature drop on the stairway.
Kella used the moment to climb to the ninety-ninth step because, for a moment, she felt the heat cool down.
Princess Elowen’s body was covered in a thin layer of white flame, announcing the awakening of her Flame Innate Body.
A few minutes after her, Madea also awakened hers, and within fifteen minutes, every last one of them awakened their flame bodies, marking the start of their dominance.
"Are you all well?" Princess Elowen asked with a smile, watching all her friends successfully awaken their flame bodies.
With a nod of confirmation, they walked past Kella, who could only stand there and wonder just what the hell had happened.
They walked past her as if the heat on the step meant nothing to them.
If only she knew that the moment the eight half-elves awakened their innate bodies, they had each gained both high-level comprehension and resistance to the flame.
Inside the tower now, aside from Kent, they were the only ones with the means to climb to the fifth level. But before then, they ate their Lotus Plum Mind Fruits.
They did not need a note telling them the fruit came from Kent.
"Kent said we should learn at least seven techniques each and then head to the fifth floor. We should hurry then."
The eight half-elves nodded to her words and then started looking for the best techniques that would suit them well.
On the outside, aside from Kent, none of the half-elves had managed to make it to the top forty. However, they’d arrived at the fourth level.
This means the ranking was about to change again.

Kent wanted to protect the half-elves, so he made sure that after today, everyone would know their names, and those who wanted to point their weapons at them would know that eight geniuses from Elarion are talents capable of dominating the world.
So instead of pointing their weapons, they would ally with them instead, and in doing so, Kent would be swimming in Soul Essence.

Kent wanted to protect the half-elves, so he made sure that after today, everyone would know their names, and those who wanted to point their weapons at them would know that eight geniuses from Elarion are talents capable of dominating the world.
So instead of pointing their weapons, they would ally with them instead, and in doing so, Kent would be swimming in Soul Essence.

chapters.title: Chapter 774: Handsome Redhead
paragraphs: (Kent’s POV - One Hour After He Fell Asleep)

On the fifth level, Kent’s body remained asleep; however, his consciousness was somewhere else. He didn’t know how it happened; however, to him, one moment he was resting at the 5th level, the next, he woke up in a weird space.
"Where in hell am I?" Kent almost shouted when he appeared atop a floating island over a sea of lava. The entire landscape was made of lava, and just looking at it made Kent’s body shudder.
He may have already boasted that, with his current flame resistance and other aspects, he would be able to jump into an active volcano and swim in the lava like a fish.
However, the truth of the matter was that he would be reduced to ash before even reaching 200 meters from its surface.
He could see the heat, and while he was safe on the floating island, stepping off it would be a disaster for him.
Kent turned and looked over the floating island; however, aside from dry land and a couple of jagged stones, there was nothing else worth noting.
There was no one, no note, or anything that pointed to the reason why he was there.
The tower also wasn’t responding to his call, so he knew he wasn’t in his real body.
This was just a realm into which his consciousness had been pulled. But then there was nobody there for the last time his consciousness was pulled; he met Chaos and Faceless.
"Maybe I am dreaming." Kent, being a simple man, came to a sudden conclusion, so he sat down and decided to rest again.

He was surrounded by death, but knowing he was protected from the heat while on the island, he chose to sleep. He sat down and lay his back on the ground, lifting his right leg to rest on his left knee.
"Though this dream is not pleasant at all. Perhaps next time I should comprehend ice; I might just end up in a fortress of solitude where the air would be much more comforting."
Kent closed his eyes and started to wait for when he would wake up from his dream.
A few hours went by, but he was still there. However, Kent knew he wouldn’t be there for long, for he knew the moment the three days were over, the tower would wake him up.
However, nothing prepared him for what happened three hours after he entered the weird realm.
At first, he thought perhaps the sun was being covered by a cloud. However, after a few moments of thought, he realized there was no sun where he was. The lava pool lit the space.
So then, why was a shield covering his face? That shouldn’t be possible.
Kent knew that much was true. So he opened his eyes, and that was when his gaze met a handsome redhead smiling down at him.
"What the f—" Kent shot up, landing a few meters from the person who stood over him. When his eyes landed on the redhead, his body shuddered.

Instinctively, Kent’s claws elongated because he couldn’t pull his sword. He went into battle stance immediately, and for a moment, he thought about charging at the figure, not out of desperation but sheer fear.

’That is a demigod.’ Kent didn’t know how he knew, but he just knew the person before him was a demigod, and judging by the way his mere presence was making him feel, he knew even his chaos blood wouldn’t be able to shield him from the danger staring at him.
"Just fear?" the handsome redhead muttered, looking strangely at Kent. Of course, Kent was also looking at him strangely.
However, the reason behind the strange looks from both of them was completely different.
Kent was looking at the handsome redhead to see if his life was in danger. He felt the aura and knew feelings like that weren’t normal.
There had to be a reason.
Of course, that was Kent’s thought, for he hadn’t felt fear, not even once, from the very moment he was sent to this world.
The only time he could have felt fear was when he, Kaizo, Veydris, and Sylara poisoned the Tyrant King in Fedora.
But even back then, instead of fear, he felt the rush to put his life in danger and dance on the edge of life and death.
However, today he felt genuine fear. That was immediately translated into hostile intent, and for that, Kent assumed the handsome redhead demigod was out for blood.

However, while Kent’s thought was his own, the demigod was having a completely different thought. In all the things he wanted to see or had seen, a mortal standing with no sign of falling to his knees at his presence wasn’t one of them.
He expected Kent not even to be able to stand up when he appeared. However, Kent not only stood up; he even activated a weapon and was ready to mess him up.
That was just too shocking, and so the demigod was taken aback.
No mortal can stand before a demigod and not drop to their knees, regardless of whether or not the demigod emits their presence. But Kent was standing there and could move freely.
This made the handsome redhead point at him, "You Dragon boy, who are you, and why can you stand my presence?"
The question was simple, straightforward, yet the answer was one that Kent knew had to be calculated.
He could sense something was supposed to have happened when the man appeared, and now that it was confirmed, he knew he had to tread carefully.
If he were to say the wrong thing, he didn’t know how that would result for him. He was not in control of the whole situation. His life is in danger now.
So, he had to answer the question with carefully chosen words and a firm resolve. If he didn’t say the right words, he might just get smoked.
However, while Kent was aware of the severity of this situation, he also didn’t feel the need to say the right words. For some reason, the craziness he inherited from Chaos was influencing him.
And while that could be managed, Kent had also told himself that he would trust himself and would never deny any part of himself. Doing so would be betraying himself.
So Chaos is crazy, and while he can choose not to be crazy too, he can’t deny himself.
But by being crazy, he knew he would say the wrong thing, and the end game would be bad for him.
’Moments like this are what we call the Three Body problem.’
’I have the means and resolve, but they are all dangerous.’
’Then again, Chaos only said he was going to the Primal Void, and when he returned, he would kill every last problem hindering Lumen, and he did.’
He only said what he meant and believed in it. That is the spirit of the Chaos Dragon.
The end game was how he wanted it to be, and now, he was faced with one roadblock, and the only thing he could think of was to brag.
’That is a demigod, but I am the Chaos Dragon... my blood is thicker than his.’
"Pay attention, Mr. Demigod, for I will not repeat myself."A grin appeared on Kent’s face. "You are honored to be in the presence of the undefeated, the most handsome, and the sane one.
I go by many names. They referred to my great self in my titles and described in my tonations. I dont sing my praises, but you can call me the Primordial Chaos Dragon."
*Rumbled*

chapters.title: Chapter 775: The One Called The Primordial Chaos Dragon. [Bonus]
paragraphs: The universe is vast and old.
It has lived for billions of years.
Endured billions of wars.
Seen grim massacres.
Tasted the metallic sourness of blood.
And cried bitter tears whenever her beloved fell.
The universe saw legends rise and fall. She saw worlds born and die.
But she also saw beauty, peace, and tranquility.
However, among all this devastation, she saw the birth and rise of one person heralded as the bringer of chaos.
He was born without a known lineage, and nobody can trace his ancestry.
Those who tried to pierce into his fate lost their fate. Those who wanted to read his destiny lost their destiny.
In the end, they called him the last of the True Primordials — beings who were born when the universe formed. They came with the universe and are one with the universe.
And so, they named him the Primordial Chaos Dragon, the first and last of his kind.
His legend is etched at the heart of the universe and echoes in its outer reaches, telling everyone of the one named the Primordial Chaos Dragon.
Such a person is no simple man. His mere name demands respect, and aside from him, nobody else can invoke it.
Lord Agni Sauron, the Flame Lord, has lived for billions of years, seeing what he could and hearing what he could hear.
However, among the many things he heard, the only thing he kept was the name of the one who once existed, whose name has been recognized by the universe.
Whenever he invokes his name with intent, the universe acknowledges him.
That name was invoked today, and the entirety of the Flame Domain, where the Flame Lord pulled into Kent, shook heavily.
The Sea of lava surged, and the floating island shuddered, chunks tearing apart.
The air grew heavy, and as all this happened, Kent stood tall, his form exuding an air of strength, dominance, and someone meant to stand above all.
The one meant to go down on his knees now stood tall, and the demigod was rather humbled.
He dropped to his knees and, for the first time in his life, paid his respect to the one who deserved it.
"This humble servant pays his respect to the Primordial Chaos Dragon, the greatest who stood above all else. The greatest of all dragons. The bringer of Chaos."
Kent stood frozen, then a grin appeared at the corner of his lips. He was frozen not from fear. This time, he was frozen in shock.
He never expected a demigod to fall to his knees and pay him respect. He, a mere mortal, was being respected by a demigod...
That’s just too much.
"Ahem," Kent cleared his throat. "You can stand up."
"Thank you, my lord." The demigod stood up, but not before thanking Kent.
"You can just call me Kent."
"I dare not. If the universe hears me dare disrespect the Primordial Chaos Dragon, according to the legends, I will be struck down and my lineage wiped out...
Though I don’t have a lineage left, I don’t dare disrespect the Primordial Chaos Dragon."

Kent scratched the back of his neck, not knowing what kind of headache he had found himself in. Just when he thought it was cool to brag about his awesome self, he landed himself in a rather unpleasant situation.

Being called by these titles didn’t sound nice in Kent’s ears. To him, being called Kent was enough. However, looking at the demigod who was now looking at him with reverence, he knew he wasn’t going to take no for an answer.
"What is your name?" Kent asked, sounding like the bigger man between the two of them.
"I am Agni Sauron, but to the rest of the universe, I am known as the Flame Lord."
"Then I will call you the Flame Lord."
"No. My lord shouldn’t do that. Referring to me by my title is an insult to you. I am not worthy to be called by the Primordial Chaos Dragon using my title."
Kent smiled, "Then why don’t we compromise? You can call me Kent, and I will call you Agni. If you call me the Primordial Chaos Dragon, I will call you the Flame Lord.
And since I’m too awesome to call you the Flame Lord, then we can all address each other by our first names. Of course, if you don’t want to use Kent, you can call me Chaos. That is my second name."
Agni went into a moment of contemplation. After weighing the demand, he was forced to accept one name, and that was Chaos.
However, as someone who had spent billions of years worshipping the Primordial Chaos Dragon, just calling Kent by his name didn’t sit well with him.
So he compromised.
"I will call you Lord Chaos or Lord Kent. That is the lowest I can go."
Kent just smiled, "I guess whatever makes you happy will do. That said, I think this is the best time to tell me why I am here.
Also, you shouldn’t worry about the universe. She can be uptight sometimes, but trust me, she wouldn’t do anything to you.
[Core of the Universe — Lady Universe POV]
Sitting at the core of the universe, Lady Universe smirked when she heard Kent refer to her as uptight. She can see and hear all he said if she wants to.
And as someone who had been paying attention to Kent’s life, her connection is always active, hearing all there is to listen to and all she wants to see.
"I will make sure I squeeze your head between my legs when I get my hands on you." A smile that celestial beings and cosmic entities would pay to see appeared on her face.
Of course, Kent had no idea there was someone perverted watching his life every passing second. Of course, this perverted person is the heart and soul of the universe.
She is the universe and everything it contains. So while Kent doesn’t know of her existence, the brat knew someone was looking after him, making sure he had the means to grow and never lack.
Kent couldn’t bring himself to think a man would do that. So he could only attribute his feelings to a lady.
If only he knew this lady was only bidding her time to sink her fangs in him.
[The Lost Temple — The Enchantress POV]
Sitting on the throne, hair carpeting the floor, the Enchantress stared at a thick, dark gold thread pulsing with potent energy.
"Who expected things to end up this way?" A smile appeared on her lips as she looked at the thread. It was the thread of fate, one belonging to the Chaos Dragon.
Just now, Kent’s fate thread grew thicker and stronger. This only happens when a person encounters something or someone that will play a significant role in their life and growth.
Kent’s fate line thickened to the point that the Enchantress had to examine it to see if any more abnormalities had occurred. But from what she had seen, nothing of the sort happened.
It was just a meeting between Kent and a dedicated fan who had done everything in his power to gather legends of Kent’s past and chose to worship him like many others.
However, while this meeting was unexpected, the outcome would shape Kent’s path toward something even the universe did not foresee.

chapters.title: Chapter 776: Finger of Destruction [Bonus]
paragraphs: Kent and Agni sat down.
He was brought into the realm he was in now for a reason. So while Kent would love to be worshipped by a demigod, he wanted to know the reason why he was there.

"First of all, I am thrilled to be talking to you now, even if this is just a strand of my consciousness. If my real body is still out there, which I know for sure it is, then soon, he will be made aware of your presence and look for you once you reach an immortal world," Agni said with a smile, causing Kent to shake his head.
’I guess I now have a demi-god fan’
"I look forward to meeting the real you one of these days. But can we get on with the main reason why I am here?"
Agni smiled and then got down to business. The faster he was done with that, the more he could learn about Kent.
"You are here because of a flame technique that I stole many years ago." Kent raised his brow, and Agni smiled, wearing a guilty expression.
"I have a reason for doing so."
"I sure would love to know why you did that, so why don’t you start sharing?"

"Of course." Agni changed his sitting posture. "So, several years back, when I had just become an Early Immortal, an ancient rift opened, and in the immortal worlds, all we do is explore ancient rifts to find treasures.
I happened to enter this rift thanks to the influence of a few friends, despite my initial hesitation. However, after I entered, we discovered it wasn’t an ordinary rift.
This one came from the Primordial Era, specifically the ancient primordial era, the time of the six true primordials.
The rift led to a chunk of the domain that used to belong to the Ancient Flame Beast King, Heliux.
He was one of the True Primordials and the creator of the legendary technique, [Finger of Destruction]. His legend is known by many and worshipped by many during the Primordial Era.
And this rift we entered led to his domain.
Of course, not everything is as simple as it appears.
While this ancient rift was initially rewarding and beneficial to us, something unexpected happened, triggering a huge battle within this domain.
It was one of the gravest battles I witnessed and ultimately participated in. However, while I could brag and say I had it easy, the truth was that the battle nearly ended me.
I nearly died. However, when things were turning grim for me, something awakened from the depths of the ancient rift, putting the battle to bed for a couple of hours.
At first, nobody recognized what had awakened, but during the awakening process, somebody read the name written on the tome.
It turns out that the tome contains the Legendary Finger of Destruction technique created by the true lord of the Flame.

You can already guess what happened. Everybody wanted to get the technique, but only one person could have it. So the battle resumed, and in the end, the tome was destroyed, or more like shattered into seven pieces," Agni smiled.
"Now, this is where I came in. Due to the chaos, I chose to run away, and I did. I wasn’t going to kill myself competing with True Immortals and Lord Immortals.
So I ran, and in the process, a chunk of the slab fell into my path. Naturally, I didn’t leave empty-handed.
However, that was a bad idea, since the moment I managed to get a chunk, I became a target. I am sure, to this day, they are still hunting me.

Of course, they will never stop hunting after me, because while the tome was divided into seven forms, I happened to get the part that contains the first form of the [Finger of Destruction] technique.
This means nobody can learn the other forms they got. Of course, many tried; some even managed to learn, but they couldn’t capture the true essence of the technique.
Even so, they somehow managed to get something out of it.

Of course, in a twisted kind of way, when I brought this technique this far, suppressing myself as a mortal to learn it, I discovered the bitter truth, one that broke me." Agni laughed again, looking at Kent.

Kent, of course, could already tell the reason he couldn’t learn the technique. It wasn’t too hard to guess. "Let me guess. To learn the technique, you must start when your flame comprehension is at the weak stage."
Agni just smiled, nodding.

The pain was evident in his eyes. He suffered only to end up with nothing. The technique that immortals, demi-gods, gods, and even the supreme hunted him down for hundreds of thousands of years turned out to be useless to him.
"To be able to learn this technique, you must meet some requirements. One of them is to be at the weak stage for both flame comprehension and resistance.
The second is to create 108,000 Flame Veins, and the last is to form seven Flame Cores.
Back then, I was already at the Immunity Resistance stage, and my comprehension was already at the Transcendent stage.
Even my Flame Veins were only 69,000 and had only formed 3 Flame Cores. I was not suited for the technique, so I did what I could to prevent it from falling into the hands of my enemies.
I buried it here with hopes that one day, somebody worthy of reaching the fifth level of the Flame Tower can give it a shot.
It has been thousands of years already, but nobody has managed to come close. The last time somebody got close was a couple of decades ago.
However, who would have thought the seventh True Primordial would appear here today? I believe I have been waiting for you to show up.
You are the primordial Chaos Dragon after all."
Kent smiled. "Say, what is the grade of this legendary technique?"
"So far as I am aware, the Finger of Destruction technique is a Primordial-grade technique, the strongest grade a skill or technique can reach in the known universe."
"Damn."
Kent felt the weight of the discovery press down on him. He always thought Celestial grade was the peak, but it turns out things are much bigger than he expected.
However, things wouldn’t be as simple as they sound. Several variables are at play here.
The first being the attainment of flame resistance and comprehension. He already has that in the bag.
However, that is the only place his brilliance stops.
The second requirement sounded like a lot of pain. He must create 108,000 flame veins, and the ultimate goal is to form 7 Flame Cores.
That is just too much even for him. However, he also understood that being given a Primordial-grade technique on a silver platter was already too much of a gift.
It wasn’t something he could ignore easily.

"If I were to embark on this journey, I suppose my flame resistance and comprehension will stagnate at the Weak stage until I manage to form the 108,000 Flame Veins and seven Flame Cores," Kent asked, and Agni nodded.

"But that is just the thing. No matter how disappointing that may sound, the end justifies the means. Forming just one Flame Core will give you so much that you can’t even start to fathom just how any of it was possible."
Kent nodded. "Tell me more about Flame Veins and Flame Cores."

So while Kent would love to be worshipped by a demigod, he wanted to know the reason why he was there.
"First of all, I am thrilled to be talking to you now, even if this is just a strand of my consciousness.

If my real body is still out there, which I know for sure it is, then soon, he will be made aware of your presence and look for you once you reach an immortal world," Agni said with a smile, causing Kent to shake his head.

His legend is known by many and worshipped by many during the Primordial Era.

Everybody wanted to get the technique, but only one person could have it.

chapters.title: Chapter 777: True Flame Path
paragraphs: Agni was more than happy to share with Kent all he knew about flame cultivation. He had been obsessed with the Primordial Chaos dragon for a very long time.

He spent years chasing down leads on the primordial Chaos Dragon. He fought unnecessary battles, be it bidding wars or actual battles, just to secure something, anything related to the primordial Chaos Dragon.
He is the definition of a die-hard fan.
So being asked by the True Primordial Chaos dragon to teach him something was already blowing his mind to bits.
Thanks to his experience walking that path, perhaps no one else was better qualified to teach Kent about flame cultivation.
"When it comes to walking the flame path, there are many aspects that must be taken into consideration. The first of them is Flame Veins.
These veins are pathways through which the essence of flames can be harnessed.
Just like how we channel spiritual qi through our meridians, the flame veins act as meridians for the flame essence.
Of course, it goes beyond that. It has many uses and several advantages.
One being, aside from merely having the means to channel the essence of flame, can also use the flame veins to channel spiritual qi.
This means that forming Flame Veins can be used for both flame-related attacks and non-flame-related attacks."
Kent raised his brow, intrigued and shocked by what he had just heard.
Agni smiled.
This was just a strand of his consciousness, but that was enough to teach Kent what he needed to know about what is required to walk the flame path.
Of course, although the full consciousness out there would do a much better job, knowing the basics wasn’t too much to worry about.
He has a complete understanding of what he was saying, and Kent can feel that.
"I know what I said may sound unbelievable, but the truth of the matter is, being in the medium world will make things like this sound unbelievable.
However, there is so much out there that when you learn about it, you will be left in a state of shock, more than you are now."
Kent was indeed shocked.
The concept of having more pathways to channel energy into attacks was one he was familiar with.
Jest had already experimented with that path.
In his quest to move past the limit of the realm of a sword King, he explored this path, and what he found was enough for Kent to believe it was possible to form more meridians.
Of course, as an alchemist, he knew things like this were possible.
However, what blew Kent’s mind now was the fact that he had just been told that flame veins could be used as pathways to channel more spiritual qi into his attacks.
That was just too much.
Having an additional ten meridians was already enough to make someone monstrous.

However, things aren’t as simple as they sound now. Things are getting much more freaky, and thinking about what would happen once one manages to form 108,000 flame veins is just too much to even think of.

If one were to achieve it, there would be 108,000 different ways to harness spiritual qi. And if that isn’t too much to comprehend its danger, then perhaps it isn’t worth the struggle to even think about such ridiculousness.
"Lord Chaos, you have to know, in the world of cultivation, you will see and hear ridiculous things such as what I have just told you.
However, you must understand that in the grand scheme of things, those who manage to seize opportunities soar above all else.
This is why you should strive to walk down the path of the flame.
Now, about the Flame Cores.

Those are much more difficult to form. But when one manages to form just one, their energy output rises. It involves channeling a large amount of flame essence and compressing it into a concentrated form.
Consider it as a secondary energy source, where, in this case, only flame energy can be stored and harnessed.
This means with a flame core at your disposal, you wouldn’t even have to worry about running out of energy at any moment.
And you have to form seven of them."
Kent smiled weakly, knowing the path set before him, though beneficial, would demand a lot. In essence, he could already see himself getting even busier than he was now.
However, upon reflection, a primordial-grade technique was at stake here. Also, although the technique sounded impressive, he could already see a completely new path opening up for him.

He could see himself channeling devastating infernal energy through thousands of pathways, unleashing world-shattering attacks. That was already more than enough for him to know he had scored a good path.
"This all sounds great, and so far, I can already see a path opening. Also, I seem to have grasped the dangers waiting for me in the high and immortal worlds.
It seems there is more than what I can see now, and that alone is enough for me to know life will soon become chaotic for me.
This is why I have decided to add the flame path to my path now. I will walk the flame path and learn the technique. After all, while it might take time, I will become much stronger in the end."
Agni nodded, very happy that Kent had decided to walk the path of the flame.

"I am happy to hear that, Lord Chaos. Right now, you will have to do things on your own, but soon, when my actual body learns of you, I am sure I will do everything in my power to provide you with resources that will hasten your path."
Kent nodded, already knowing that one of these days, he would meet the true demigod named Agni, who had been eager to meet him, the primordial Chaos Dragon.
"So, what do I do now?" Kent asked, and Agni extended his hand, causing two scrolls to appear.

"These are the methods to create Flame Veins and Flame Cores. They will guide you to start walking the path of the flame. However, you must form at least 20,000 flame veins before attempting to form a core.
Also, you don’t have to worry about your path and comprehension rising. You just need to find the Flame Binding Pill and take it. It will hold your path for five years.

The tier should be at least nine, and you should take it before you learn these two methods. Of course, if you manage to form seven cores and create 108,000 veins within five years, you can take another pill called the Flame Release Pill.
They may be rare in your world, but once you get to a high world, you can easily find some of these pills."
"Thank you, Agni. I will be sure to pay you back when we meet again."
Agni smiled, "Merely meeting the primordial Chaos Dragon is enough for me. Also, the two techniques for creating the flame core and vein will be waiting for you on the outside."
Kent nodded, then started asking more questions about the universe out there waiting for him. Agni, of course, was more than happy to tell him all he wanted to know.
Soon, a day had passed since Kent and the others entered the tower. Outside, everyone was stunned, staring at the display board with expressions frozen in place.
The outcome many expected wasn’t happening at all. Some names that weren’t well-known or popular now populated the top rankings.
It just made no sense to all those looking at the display board.

chapters.title: Chapter 778: Tower Closed
paragraphs: Eventually, only one hour remained before the tower closed.
But a lot had happened.
First, those destined to fail still couldn’t even comprehend a heavenly grade flame art. No matter how hard they tried, they couldn’t accomplish it.
It may be harsh to say, but spending resources on such people would be a waste, for they lack the natural talent to even try without external help.
While some eventually managed to learn at least one technique, others failed even to scratch the surface.
However, away from there, some managed to reach the second level and even the third level.
The main fun, however, happened on the 4th level.
Some years back, only one person managed to reach that level. This time, 24 managed to get there, and some even went beyond.
Princess Elowen and her friends were told to learn seven techniques each by Kent, for he had helped them reach Tier 12 in soul cultivation before they entered the tower.
So, thanks to their souls enlarging to a rather proportioned degree, they managed to complete their task 36 hours into the 72 hours they would be spending inside the tower.
By the time they each comprehended the seven Mythic grade techniques, the first ten ranks on the display board were occupied by the half-elves.
Kent was in the first spot, with Princess Freya sitting in the second spot, having mastered eight mythic grade techniques.
She is naturally gifted, so comprehending eight mythic-grade techniques was sufficient for someone of her standing.
From the third to the tenth were taken by the half-elves, and the eleventh was taken by Helga, Princess Freya’s friend and maid.
She is the daughter of the queen’s maid and has been friends with the dwarven princess from childhood. They are inseparable in a way, and their talent is almost on par.

Surprisingly, the twelfth spot was taken by Kella, who was so shocked that she didn’t know what to say. She managed to reach the 4th level; however, what she never expected was learning six mythic-grade techniques.

In fact, on the outside, the Elven queen was even more shocked than her. She didn’t know much about Kella, but seeing her name there made her happy to some extent, although not to the extent she had wanted to be.
She expected her geniuses to dominate the charts, but the display board wasn’t on her side at all. Of course, Kella tried, but she couldn’t compete against Kent’s side.
The remaining names were claimed by the seven survivalists who, against all odds, managed to reach the 4th level.
However, when all was done at the 4th level for the eight half-elves, they were ready to head to the 5th level. Kent told them to head there once they finished the 4th level.
So they did, and that was when things began to change. It was unexpected, but it happened anyway.
Princess Freya asked if she could go with the half-elves.
She saw how they arrived at the 4th level and, as someone whose intelligence was now much sharper than before, she recognized that all eight half-eleves weren’t simple at all.
So she gambled, and to her surprise, Princess Elowen accepted her offer, even extending it to her friend, Helga.
However, one person nobody expected to be taken was Kella, who wasn’t even sure why they had taken her.
She merely wanted to try her luck, for at that moment, she didn’t see herself as an elf; she saw herself as a daughter who wanted to make a good life for herself and her father.
She wanted to do what Kent told her to, and so she took a big swing and it caught a fish.
Her request was sincere, and when she was done asking, she received only one answer: "Ok."

Princess Elowen accepted her offer, and for a moment, tears fell from her eyes. However, she recovered, and that was when the eight half-elves began helping the three loads they had taken with them to the 5th level.
As they climbed to the 5th level, Agni allowed Kent to watch. The sight brought a smile to his face.
He never expected the half-elves to be that generous, even going out of their way to take along an elf.
However, after six hours of climbing, they all reached the 5th level.
That was when they discovered Kent’s sleeping body. Initially, they thought something had happened to him, but upon closer inspection, they saw he was just asleep.
This left their jaws hanging by a thread. However, after recovering, they went to inspect the techniques they would be learning.
In the end, all eleven of them found a technique to master, and for hours they were at it.
[One Hour Before The Flame Tower Closed]

"Thank you, Agni. I have learned a great deal over the past few hours. I will be sure to apply them all, and perhaps the next time we meet, we can go on adventures together," Kent said, shaking Agni’s hand.
"I am glad I was helpful," Agni replied.

"Before you leave, take this." Agni handed a token to Kent. "It is the core of the Flame Tower. Since I have completed my mission for leaving my consciousness here, the moment the tower closes, I will cease to exist here.

When that happens, the tower will be left masterless. That means it won’t open again. However, I already realize the people of your world gain a lot from it, so I want you to become the master of the Tower."
Kent smiled upon hearing that. He was already a master of a much more powerful tower. But this is also good.
"I will be happy to take over from you."
"Great. Also, in the future, if you have some Flame Arts, you can leave them for future generations to benefit. You can even change the rules, like when the tower awakens and who can enter.
That said, it is time for you to go back.
I know we will meet again one day because I will look for you."
"Take care, then. And be mindful of those chasing after you. When you find yourself in a situation you can’t handle, invoke my name.
I am sure I will find my way to help you. And don’t worry, the universe will not hurt you. So you have my permission to use my name."
Agni went down on his knees and bowed to Kent. "Thank you, Lord Chaos. I am flattered. I will be sure to use your name when I truly need it."
Until then, see you later, Lord Chaos."
Kent felt his vision blur, then he woke up back inside the 5th level.
When he opened his eyes, his gaze landed on eleven people sitting on the ground looking back at him.
But aside from them, four things were hovering before him. One was the small token he would be using to claim ownership of the Flame Tower.

The second and third were the techniques he needed to learn to create Flame Veins and Flame Cores. The last, of course, was a piece of the tome containing the first form of the Finger of Destruction technique.
’I will get into this later,’ Kent waved his hand, and all four items entered his tower storage. He looked at his friends and the three new faces with them.
"So, how many divine techniques were you able to learn?"
Everyone smiled.
"We could only manage one, but that is enough to shape our futures," Princess Elowen answered.
"That isn’t too bad. That said, we should be ready to enter the sect in a week. The future starts there."
An hour later, the tower closed, and everyone was transported out.

Of course, Kella tried, but she couldn’t compete against Kent’s side.
The remaining names were claimed by the seven survivalists who, against all odds, managed to reach the 4th level.
However, when all was done at the 4th level for the eight half-elves, they were ready to head to the 5th level.
Kent told them to head there once they finished the 4th level.
So they did, and that was when things began to change.
It was unexpected, but it happened anyway.
Princess Freya asked if she could go with the half-elves.
She saw how they arrived at the 4th level and, as someone whose intelligence was now much sharper than before, she recognized that all eight half-eleves weren’t simple at all.
So she gambled, and to her surprise, Princess Elowen accepted her offer, even extending it to her friend, Helga.
However, one person nobody expected to be taken was Kella, who wasn’t even sure why they had taken her.
She merely wanted to try her luck, for at that moment, she didn’t see herself as an elf; she saw herself as a daughter who wanted to make a good life for herself and her father.
She wanted to do what Kent told her to, and so she took a big swing and it caught a fish.
Her request was sincere, and when she was done asking, she received only one answer: "Ok."
Princess Elowen accepted her offer, and for a moment, tears fell from her eyes.
However, she recovered, and that was when the eight half-elves began helping the three loads they had taken with them to the 5th level.
As they climbed to the 5th level, Agni allowed Kent to watch.
The sight brought a smile to his face.
He never expected the half-elves to be that generous, even going out of their way to take along an elf.
However, after six hours of climbing, they all reached the 5th level.
That was when they discovered Kent’s sleeping body.
Initially, they thought something had happened to him, but upon closer inspection, they saw he was just asleep.
This left their jaws hanging by a thread.
However, after recovering, they went to inspect the techniques they would be learning.
In the end, all eleven of them found a technique to master, and for hours they were at it.
[One Hour Before The Flame Tower Closed]
"Thank you, Agni.
I have learned a great deal over the past few hours.
I will be sure to apply them all, and perhaps the next time we meet, we can go on adventures together," Kent said, shaking Agni’s hand.
"I am glad I was helpful," Agni replied.
"Before you leave, take this." Agni handed a token to Kent.
"It is the core of the Flame Tower.
Since I have completed my mission for leaving my consciousness here, the moment the tower closes, I will cease to exist here.
When that happens, the tower will be left masterless.
That means it won’t open again.
However, I already realize the people of your world gain a lot from it, so I want you to become the master of the Tower."
Kent smiled upon hearing that.
He was already a master of a much more powerful tower.
But this is also good.
"I will be happy to take over from you."
"Great.
Also, in the future, if you have some Flame Arts, you can leave them for future generations to benefit.
You can even change the rules, like when the tower awakens and who can enter.
That said, it is time for you to go back.
I know we will meet again one day because I will look for you."
"Take care, then.
And be mindful of those chasing after you.
When you find yourself in a situation you can’t handle, invoke my name.
I am sure I will find my way to help you.
And don’t worry, the universe will not hurt you.
So you have my permission to use my name."
Agni went down on his knees and bowed to Kent.
"Thank you, Lord Chaos.
I am flattered.
I will be sure to use your name when I truly need it."
Until then, see you later, Lord Chaos."
Kent felt his vision blur, then he woke up back inside the 5th level.
When he opened his eyes, his gaze landed on eleven people sitting on the ground looking back at him.
But aside from them, four things were hovering before him.
One was the small token he would be using to claim ownership of the Flame Tower.
The second and third were the techniques he needed to learn to create Flame Veins and Flame Cores.
The last, of course, was a piece of the tome containing the first form of the Finger of Destruction technique.
’I will get into this later,’ Kent waved his hand, and all four items entered his tower storage.
He looked at his friends and the three new faces with them.
"So, how many divine techniques were you able to learn?"
Everyone smiled.
"We could only manage one, but that is enough to shape our futures," Princess Elowen answered.
"That isn’t too bad.
That said, we should be ready to enter the sect in a week.
The future starts there."
An hour later, the tower closed, and everyone was transported out.

chapters.title: Chapter 779: Aftermath [Bonus]
paragraphs: Kent and everyone who entered the tower were ejected, and the large doors of the tower closed, sealing it for another three years.
Cheers rang out from those who managed to master at least one flame art. Their happiness was palpable.
Of course, they should be happy. What they had accomplished was something that would shape their futures forever.
They were delighted to finally have a chance to join the sect, which would continue to help them grow beyond their wildest expectations.
Essentially, learning even a heavenly grade technique had opened doors for them.
However, while some were celebrating, others were shedding tears because they couldn’t even learn a single technique.
That was their loss, for they now have no chance of even taking the sect entrance exams, let alone entering to grow further.
Their one chance to change their lives was now taken away by their inability to learn even a single technique.
Of course, those who manage to make progress are now smiling, knowing in 7 days, they will be embarking on a new journey, one that will see them grow beyond their imaginations.
Then again, although they managed to secure a slot to enter the sect, not all would make it, for another obstacle lay ahead of them.
There are the sect entrance exams that will determine who gets to enter and those who will be going back empty-handed.
Looking at the display board, their smiles painted their faces. At least, now that they have a chance, they would give it their all to enter the sect.
Kent, of course, was sitting at the top, having mastered 12 Divine-grade techniques. His dominance was as plain as day to everyone.
Mastering 12 Divine-grade techniques is too much for someone like him to manage per the expectations of others. But he did manage it, and the outcome is already too much for anyone to understand.
Of course, he wasn’t the only one.
In the second spot was Princess Freya of the Dwarven race. The cute and short beauty managed to learn eight Mythic-grade techniques and a Divine-grade technique.
That is just too much if her score were to be compared to that of the Pill Princess, who only managed to learn two.

Of course, the fruit Kent gave her helped her learn the techniques, but even without that, she had the means to learn at least three, which already shows that her potential is much bigger than the Pill Princess.
So, Kent already planted the first domino in getting to the pill princess by making Freya even more impressive.
Then came the third spot, occupied by Princess Elowen, who mastered seven Mythic-grade techniques and one Divine-grade technique.
The 4th down to the 10th were all half-elves. The 11th was Princess Freya’s friend, Helga, and on the 12th was Kella, who managed to learn six Mythic-grade techniques and a Divine-grade technique.
It was both her fortune and luck to meet someone like Kent. He had shaped her life in ways that aiming to become one of the pompous royals wouldn’t be able to compare to her now.
The seven survivalists took the remaining spots from the 13th to the 19th.
The outcome predicted by everyone was just not what was showing on the display board.
This had changed, and it was now clear who would earn the rewards from the sect and who would achieve significant success among this year’s newly accepted soon-to-be disciples.
Elder Lance flew into the air and looked at everyone, eyes lingering on Kent much longer before addressing the crowd.
"Congratulations, everyone. You’ve all done a great job entering the Flame Tower and coming out with techniques that will shape your futures.
First of all, you should take pride in your achievements. For the first time since this tower was discovered, not only have 24 people reached the 4th level, but 12 have even made it to the 5th level.
That is something you all, regardless of your ranking, should be proud of.

Second, I know you all are aware of the outcome of your achievements. According to the Supreme Immortal Sect’s rules, those who manage to learn a technique will be granted a chance to take the sect’s entrance exams.
That will happen a week from now, so be ready. You will be transported to the sect a week from today.
Lastly, as promised before the start of the trial, the first, second, and third spots will be awarded by the sect. A week from today, your rewards will be delivered.
However, I have something else to say." Elder Lance looked at everyone and smiled.

The arrogance he felt when he first arrived was now replaced by some form of respect as he looked at the various faces that managed to change his expectations of what was said about the world of Sonox.
He was told people from this world are trash. The sect doesn’t hold them in high esteem.
Unless one manages to demonstrate their brilliance through either the Flame Tower or the ancient battlefield of Parting, or perhaps they are royals, entering the sect is nearly impossible.
But now, he was proven wrong.
This was why he knew the elders at the sect would have a hard time coming to terms with what had been achieved.
"Those of you who managed to learn at least one technique, make sure the next six days are all about gaining a deeper understanding of it.
Go through the forms you’ve already mastered and be sure to relearn them, gain a better understanding, and, if possible, add another form to it.
The entrance exams will be challenging, because the sect only takes in those with potential. You’ve already proven you have some potential, so prepare well."
His words resonated in everyone’s head. However, he wasn’t done. He moved toward the half-elves, specifically Cyran, Arion, and Helyra.

"You three have proven that, against all odds, age is just a number. This is why, even though the sect only accepts those who are 100 years old or younger through the flame tower, you three will be an exception.
You three managed not only to learn seven mythic-grade techniques, but also you even learned a divine-grade technique. That is admirable.
Representing the supreme immortal sect, I am pleased to extend an official invitation to you three. A week from today, you are welcome to join everyone and participate in the sect entrance exams."
"Thank you," the three said, nodding as smiles played on their lips.
"Looks like I won’t be using my slot to invite you three after I become a core disciple in a year," Kent said, just loud enough for Elder Lance to hear.
He raised his brow but said nothing. He moved back, and after waiting for the Flame Tower to dive back into the sea of lava, the void opened, and the three of them vanished.
The moment they left, everyone turned their attention toward Kent and the half-elves. Some held hostile intents while others wore looks of admiration.
A few minutes later, some started leaving. They wanted to get down to the bottom of things, so they left. The elves left first, for their shame at falling behind the half-elves was just too much.
The demons left second, followed by the dragons, then the beasts, and eventually the dwarves. However, before leaving, Princess Freya and her friend Helga came to thank Kent.
Once they were gone, the half-elves also left.
