chapters.title: Chapter 790: Hidden Secret of the Dungeon
paragraphs: [Planet Hular - Dream Human Continent: Dream City. Emperor Yuval’s Palace]
"Emperor Yuval, we have news." An old human with pure yellow hair and an energetic body said, running into a large hall designed using the finest jade.
It looks grand and graceful, housing some of the finest and most beautiful flowers in the universe.
"Come on, Meric. You are older than I. So, there is no need to run here with your weak bones." A handsome man, also with yellow hair, sitting on a throne, said, a smile gracing his lips.
Meric smiled, but he held a serious expression, unlike the Emperor, who was in the mood to have some fun.
Of course, he is capable of having some fun, for he is Emperor Yuval, the Emperor of all races in Hular.
He shook his head and smiled, knowing this particular Elder in his council was particularly serious about his job.
"Go ahead, Meric. What happened?"
"My Emperor, the Unbreakable City has been destroyed."
"What?" Emperor Yuval’s voice echoed throughout the city like thunder. Everyone who heard him froze for a moment, an invincible force restraining them.
They were released the next second as the voice of their Emperor vanished. Of course, when they were freed, they could sense the change in the air, which means the emperor wasn’t calm at the moment.
That was the extent of his power as the emperor of the world of Hular.
"What did you just say?"
"The Unbreakable City has been destroyed, and every last Tiger was killed. Not even a single one of them was left alive to tell the tale.
I just received word from the Desert Humans who said they felt an explosion, and within an hour, when they got there, the battle was over and the perpetrators were long gone.
According to their report, aside from a couple of 50 thousand dead bodies, the rest were reduced to ash, their bones turning to dust.
If it were the Elves who reported, I would have doubted them for they love to exaggerate, but the Desert humans are different."

"How? How were the walls broken? Who has the strength to break those walls in the Alliance?. Who even had the means to kill that many tigers in under an hour?" Emperor Yuval asked, sitting back on his throne.
Planet Hular is the strongest of the many planets in the Kevlar Planetary Alliance. It is a high world, inhabited by three races: the Dream Humans, the Elves, and the Desert Humans.
Of course, they weren’t the only inhabitants. It was just that in the Kevlar planetary Alliance, only the three races were recognised.
This was because, in the past, there were seven races: the Tigerkin, the Batkin, the Lionkin, the Goatkin, the two human races, and the Elves.
The four beastkin were known as the four ancient beast races, with the Tigerkin being the strongest among them.
However, 50,000 years ago, the Tigerkin slaughtered every last one of the Goatkin, Lionkin, and Batkin, and then sealed themselves in an Unbreakable City.
Emperor Yuval, the leader of the Dream Humans, the Elves, and the Desert Humans, tried many times to break the wall and kill the tigers hiding behind it.

Of course, while the tigerkin kill their fellow beasts, making it not part of his business, as an emperor, he knew for a fact that if the tigers were allowed to keep living, they would one day surpass him and come for his people.
He couldn’t allow that to happen.

So for the past 50,000 years, he had tried many times to break the walls, but he couldn’t. Eventually, he gave up, but now he had received word that the tigers were gone, and the walls he could not break were no longer standing.
"Who would have this much strength to break those walls? Even people from the Jiko and Hulap Alliances couldn’t break them."
"Does this mean an immortal has appeared in this world?" Emperor Yuval wondered.
Meric looked at the emperor and shook his head.
He was one of the many who tried to break down the walls. As a Spirit Lord, Meric held some strength in him. But even so, he couldn’t make a dent in the wall, no matter how many times he struck it.
Even the king, who had already reached the 8th level of the Heavenly Ascension realm—just a step away from reaching the sacred Empyrean realm—tried but could only create shockwaves.
Hearing that the same walls were now broken made them wonder just what or who could have done that.
’Who could have that much attack power? Are they a threat to us? Are they a threat to the Emperor?’ Meric’s mind was running wild.
If only he knew that the attack Camilla used could kill a Root Immortal and even injure a Spirit Immortal, he would probably stop thinking and let nature run its course.
Initially, Camilla, without Lynn’s help, could only use five rings to power her ’Point Of No Return’ skill.
However, even that was enough to kill a Spirit Sovereign and injure a Spirit Lord.
So adding 95 more rings to it made it a different kind of skill—one that has no grade. And she wasn’t the only one who had that kind of skill.

Just like how Val can call down the divine power of the Moon Goddess, the rest of her sisters and the rest of the legion have something like that. But the cooldown time was just too long to use it casually.
Those skills are gradeless, meaning they grow with them and will continue to improve in the future.
It was their Plan E for when Plans A, B, C, and D failed.
So using it to win easily was not an option.
Now, Camilla used an even more powerful form of her skill, and the shock would soon rock not only Planet Hular but the whole of the Kevlar Planetary Alliance.
What happened was one they didn’t see coming.
Meanwhile, what was even more bizarre was what Kent sensed. He sensed he was in a high world on the third floor of the dungeon. The feeling was plain as day to him when he paid attention.
He had been to Fedora, so he knew how the spiritual energy in the air felt.
While he wasn’t sure at first, when he finally managed to calm himself down and sensed it, he knew he wasn’t mistaken. He was indeed in a high world, and the feeling was undeniable.
It turned out he was right.
But since that was the case, what does it mean then?
He was supposed to be in the dungeon, but it turned out that he and his team had been transported to a high world.
That alone was enough to realize the danger Kent’s legion was in or would face should they continue to climb the floors.
Dungeons are designed in such a way that every floor has a defined power level of beasts or beings they will be fighting. However, the third floor didn’t have that power structure.
This only means that the dungeon is not just a dungeon, but something else entirely.
It can even be said that it is a doorway to other worlds with predefined missions and tasks he and his team must complete.

But if that was the case, then how does it explain the fact that while Kent and his team were still in the city, and thousands of Desert people going through the destroyed city on Planet Hular, couldn’t see each other?
They were occupying the same space, but in a way, they couldn’t see each other.

chapters.title: Chapter 791: Self-Blame [Bonus]
paragraphs: [Three Minutes After Clearing the Third Floor - Just Outside the Unbreakable City]
Kent flew toward the direction of his team, who were feeling down despite having cleared the third floor as they had wanted.
Every last tiger was dead, and even the strange hellhound now stood tall and loomed over everyone since Veera had turned it into her undead.
Of course, their mood came from the fact that they had to abandon Plan A and go with Plan B, allowing Val to use her goddess form.
Before entering the dungeon, they came up with five plans.
Four of the five plans were ironed out to the last detail.
The first plan, dubbed Plan A, was simply for them to go into battle in their human forms, using their skills and wit to win at all costs.
It was a straightforward plan where those who complemented each other, such as Kaizo and Unity, would work together to kill and ensure all adversaries were taken care of.
It was that simple.
They used it on the first and second floors, and it worked flawlessly. However, upon reaching the third floor, it was proven that Plan A was inadequate.
They couldn’t possibly kill a Spirit Lord, not one that had mutated and had been eating the life force of the tigers for 50,000 years.
Even so, they came close, and had it not been for Kent’s battle with the Tiger King, things wouldn’t have ended like they did.
However, the plan wasn’t for Kent to handle the bigger threats.
Inside Plan A, they had a sub-plan in place where, when a major threat arose, Kaizo, Irina, and Veydris would handle it.
That was until even the eight new undead were added. Even so, with over 60,000 dangerous tigers against them, they knew dividing their team would be a bad move.

Aside from that, even if Kaizo, Veydris, and Irina were enough to handle the Spirit Lord, they would have to use their Gradeless skills, which, in this context, would mean they would fail Plan A regardless.
The idea behind this plan was for them to test their limits using a limited part of their strength. They created the plan as a guide and rule, but it seems they failed to meet their own expectations.
So, they adopted Plan B, and that’s what happened, souring their mood.
Val used her goddess form to handle the threat, and Alina used one of the seven Tier 18 Arrays her Primordial Spirits gave her to protect herself and her sister before she regressed.
The Odyssey of Death was one of the seven. It requires tremendous energy just to activate it. The power the ladies unleashed was but 10% of its true might.
To bring out its true might, they need a large amount of Spirit Crystals, or thirty Spirit Lords channeling their energy into the one that will activate the formation.
Even so, they would only be able to hold it for ten minutes. So it was a done deal when they activated it.
This also meant they lost despite ultimately winning.
Alina sat, channeling energy from Spirit Crystals given to them by her sister Vexthra before entering the dungeon.
Her sisters were doing the same.
After a few seconds, she looked at Kent hovering in the air over the city. Recalling how Camilla used more than she could handle to carve a path for them, a dull look appeared in her eyes.
"I am weak. If I had been just two minutes faster, my formation would have been complete, and none of this would have happened." Everyone turned toward her.
Unity rested her hand on her shoulder. "You are not weak, Alina. You just wanted to use the moment to train your speed, but who would have expected a Spirit Lord to appear all of a sudden?"
"Unity is right. Your profession requires you to spend more time in battles to know which and what Array to draw and which formation is needed.

You were terrific on the first and second floors. Don’t let this setback bring your spirit down," Elsa said, walking toward the busty beauty who knew everything had rested on her shoulders, but she had failed.
Among her sisters, she lacks the talent and physical ability for combat, especially in close combat. Her own skill is formation and arrays.
They were her primary attacks.
The moment her formation comes together, the battle will be as good as done. However, it takes her some time to get into her groove.
In the recently concluded battle, she made a mistake and had to restart the process from the beginning. She is perfect in looks, but even perfect beauties make mistakes.
In her case, the mistake cost them a chance to see just how much they can handle a battle with a Spirit Lord as an opponent among thousands of Spirit Kings and Emperors.
"Still, had it not been for the mistake I made, I wouldn’t have cost us the battle." Alina stood up and bowed in apology to her friends and sisters.
"I promise to do better next time. I won’t make a mistake next time." Tears fell from her eyes before she vanished into the tower, and then she entered her grid space to cry in silence.
Kent saw all this and, for a moment, his heart shook.
’Why are they trying so hard to prove themselves to me? Camilla did the same, and now she is in a coma for who knows how long. Now Alina too feels like she has let me down.’
He looked at everyone and could see they felt the same as Alina. The only ones with a calmer expression were the eight new undead and Veydris, who couldn’t express emotions.
The speech Kent had prepared suddenly felt inadequate.
He needed to add something spicier to it to calm their nerves and reassure them that they had done better than he expected.
Of course, they wouldn’t believe him, so a new idea appeared in his mind, one that he knew would solve their problems.
He waved his hand, and everyone vanished into the tower, appearing in the legion tower. He vanished and appeared in the harem tower.
Soon, he was in the glasshouse where Vexthra was seated, staring at the sleeping body of Camilla. Even as a goddess, she was feeling so many emotions that she didn’t know how to handle them.
In a way, learning to become human was affecting her in ways she never knew possible. If she managed to isolate and understand all these emotions, her progress would see a significant leap.
"How is she?" Kent asked the moment he arrived in the room.
"She is well. All internal injuries are healed now. The only thing left is for her to wake up. For that, even if I use my godpowers, it wouldn’t do anything to her.
She would have to wake up on her own, and I will be here when she does."
Kent clenched his fist and gritted his teeth, hearing even a goddess doesn’t have what it takes to wake Camilla up. The tower estimates she would be out for half a year or perhaps an entire year.
So she will be sleeping for a while.
Vexthra held his hand, sensing that the dragon was about to blame himself.
"It isn’t your fault, Kent. It was her choice, and you have to respect that. All of us would do that." She smiled.
"In case you are not aware, we want to be useful. She had her moment, and now, I am sure when she wakes up, she will feel accomplished.
So instead of feeling sad, be happy, your 18 beautiful wives who would do anything to help you."

chapters.title: Chapter 792: Kent’s Overpowered Emotions [Bonus]
paragraphs: Kent stood there, staring at the body of his wife sleeping peacefully on the bed.
Hearing what Vexthra said, he couldn’t help shaking his head. To him, his wives were treasures he held dear to his heart.
They made his life complete, so seeing one of them hurt and the other heartbroken made him feel like a failure.
"You all are perfect. I don’t need you proving yourselves to me to see that. I can see you all, so why go to such extreme lengths just to make me want to see you?"
Kent asked, and Vexthra smiled.
"Because we love you and want to do everything for you. Why do you think we wanted to take the dungeon off your hands so you could go out there and handle your business?
We wanted to take as many loads as you carry off your shoulders, for we are your wives and that is our role.
We aren’t just housewives or bed warmers. We are warriors, and for that, we would do everything in our power to make sure your dreams come true."
"How about your dreams? Dont you have to make them come true too?"
Vexthra’s smile blossomed into a small, loving laugh. "Our dream is to see your dreams come true. Our dream is to see you happy, fulfilled, and above all else, loved.
It may sound unusual to you to hear a group of beautiful women share the same dream.
I know it’s weird; however, that’s our dream—every last one of us. So, whenever you’re out facing danger, know that we are here, just a snap away to come to your aid.
You may be strong, Kent, but with us by your side, you will be unstoppable.
So instead of saying it, be happy that we are here for you. We are not going anywhere, nor do we plan on abandoning you. We need you, and you need us."
Vexthra stood up and hugged the big softy, who had become emotional, tears falling from his eyes. The last time Kent cried was when his mom died.
Since then, he had never known tears, but today, he couldn’t hold back his emotions.
’What did I do to deserve all this love? Do I even deserve this much love, dedication, and commitment? Am I even worthy of being loved this much?’
His emotions were in turmoil, unsure of what to think. Just a little over three years ago, he was but a lonely 34-year-old with nothing but hate buried deep in his heart.
He had nobody in his life, for he was incapable of feeling love. He couldn’t feel emotions. He was unworthy of being loved.
But now, he had not only one, but eighteen women willing to do everything they could to see him happy. That is just too much for someone like him not to feel something.
Being loved that deeply was just too much for him to handle. However, Kent’s emotional outburst turns out to have caused a much bigger disaster than anyone would have expected.
[Core of the Universe - Lady Universe’s POV]
The beauty sitting at the core of the universe heard all Vexthra said to Kent, and for a moment, something broke in her.
She was a cosmic being, someone born from the energy that the universe was created from. She was the core of the universe.
Although the universe behaves on its own, at its core is her. She is the heart and soul.
Aomeone like her was incapable of feeling love for anyone. Doing so would make her biased. This was why, for years, she remained the emotionless, calculative person the universe was supposed to be.
However, that all shattered when a certain dragon came into existence. At first, she felt skeptical about approaching him; however, she did, and that was when everything changed for her.
Of course, back then, she was incapable of loving.
She was incapable of expressing her love.

However, when her life was threatened, when the universe was threatened, when everything was becoming undone, this dragon stood by her, made sure she was protected. When it came to it, he gave his life without any hesitation to ensure she was safe.
That moment was when she fell in love for the first time. Ever since then, she had been following him in the many lives he had led.
She saw him love, live, and die on his own terms.
However, even through it all, her heart never shook, not even once.
But for the first time after watching him, following his life and doing all she could for him, her heart shook and broke watching Kent cry.
Hearing all Vexthra said and hearing all Kent thought about himself, she felt his pain, and that broke her.
"Nania, I don’t have to tell you, but crying is not an option. You can’t cry. You saw what happened the last time I cried. You saw the damage that was caused. So please, sister, don’t cry."
The enchantress’s voice entered the core, ensuring the emotional universe didn’t cry. Who knew the damage she would cause if she were to shed even a single tear?
"I can’t hold it, Diana, I just can’t."
"This is a problem." The enchantress, also known as Diana, appeared at the core of the universe and took Nania’s hand.
"Listen to me, Nania, you are the heart and soul of the universe. You are a cosmic being. You can’t express emotion through crying.
Doing so will cause more harm than good. So for his sake, for everyone’s sake, find a way to hold back your emotion."
If she were made of flesh like humans, she would have long shed her tears, but as a cosmic being, crying just one tear can take years, perhaps centuries.
So, if she doesn’t hold her emotions firm now, she will destroy more worlds in a couple of years, and since this was related to Kent, perhaps months from now or even weeks.
It could be any moment.
The universe cried before, on multiple occasions, but it wasn’t from her heart and soul. This was a first, and that alone is more than the universe needs at the moment.
Thankfully, her tears didn’t fall from her eyes. Without even knowing it, four people cried their tears.
Inside the mountain garden, Gaia, Akira, and Dori cried tears meant for their mother. It was the emotion they had never felt before.
Inside the legion tower, Unity also cried. She didn’t know why, but all of a sudden, she felt an emotion so pure that it overwhelmed her, causing her to burst into tears.

She, along with the three cosmic entities, cried, and the repercussions will be paid in due time. Three cosmic beings and a goddess, whose story the universe cannot wait to tell, cried when they shouldn’t have.
While the damage wasn’t immediate, it will soon come knocking.
After the emotional moment shared with Vexthra, Kent regained his composure and stayed with Camilla for a few hours before heading to the Legion Tower.
He had to ensure the rest of his wives and legion didn’t get depressed over their loss.
Of course, if anyone heard they had lost because they couldn’t win a battle with their first plan but actually won with the second of five plans, they would probably curse them for being petty.
But even so, he had to make sure they didn’t turn into a bunch of heartbroken dolls. He had his own plans, and babysitting them wasn’t one of them.

sentences.text: Kent stood there, staring at the body of his wife sleeping peacefully on the bed.
Hearing what Vexthra said, he couldn’t help shaking his head.
To him, his wives were treasures he held dear to his heart.
They made his life complete, so seeing one of them hurt and the other heartbroken made him feel like a failure.
"You all are perfect.
I don’t need you proving yourselves to me to see that.
I can see you all, so why go to such extreme lengths just to make me want to see you?"
Kent asked, and Vexthra smiled.
"Because we love you and want to do everything for you.
Why do you think we wanted to take the dungeon off your hands so you could go out there and handle your business?
We wanted to take as many loads as you carry off your shoulders, for we are your wives and that is our role.
We aren’t just housewives or bed warmers.
We are warriors, and for that, we would do everything in our power to make sure your dreams come true."
"How about your dreams?
Dont you have to make them come true too?"
Vexthra’s smile blossomed into a small, loving laugh.
"Our dream is to see your dreams come true.
Our dream is to see you happy, fulfilled, and above all else, loved.
It may sound unusual to you to hear a group of beautiful women share the same dream.
I know it’s weird; however, that’s our dream—every last one of us.
So, whenever you’re out facing danger, know that we are here, just a snap away to come to your aid.

We are not going anywhere, nor do we plan on abandoning you.

Am I even worthy of being loved this much?’
His emotions were in turmoil, unsure of what to think.
Just a little over three years ago, he was but a lonely 34-year-old with nothing but hate buried deep in his heart.
He had nobody in his life, for he was incapable of feeling love.
He couldn’t feel emotions.
He was unworthy of being loved.
But now, he had not only one, but eighteen women willing to do everything they could to see him happy.
That is just too much for someone like him not to feel something.
Being loved that deeply was just too much for him to handle.

chapters.title: Chapter 793: Going On Retreat
paragraphs: "Alright. Listen up. In battles, there are winners and losers. Either option is acceptable if it happens under the right conditions.
You all fought bravely, and while the outcome you anticipated wasn’t the one you got, the takeaway here is you won. None of you died or were even injured.

You won in the end, and that should be enough to cheer you up. So, instead of feeling down, lighten up. There are more fights left to be fought, and I want you all to be in perfect shape when the time comes."
Kent said, his tone commanding when he appeared in the legion tower. They were all in the legion tower when he arrived.
Just as he had expected, the space was filled with dull energy; everyone felt down, as if they had just run a marathon.
He expected them to lighten up after a few hours, but they still held a sour and dull look in their eyes when he arrived.
Kaizo, who was always cheerful and ready for battle, even looked more dull than the rest. The failure stung like a knife to the heart.
"I don’t think you understand, master. This was supposed to be something we did without you. We were supposed to face the Spirit Sovereign instead of you.
So imagine what would have happened if you weren’t there to handle him, and instead, the team we had from the start was the one we used to face him.
What would have happened if I, Veydris, and Irina were handling the Tiger King when the Hellhound appeared?

We already failed when you joined the battle from the start. And this is because, without our flashy skills and overpowered bloodlines, we are basically weak by all standards." Kaizo made his feelings known.
And looking at the rest of his friends, they all shared his view.
What he said was indeed true.
Had it not been for Kent taking the Tiger King all by himself, the outcome would have come much faster than what had happened.
In a way, they were doomed to fail.
Of course, with Elyndra joining Kaizo, Veydris, and Irina, they would have ultimately managed to kill the Tiger King. But that would have taken them at least an hour to handle him.

This means that during their battle, the Hellhound would have appeared, and a new team would have had to be deployed to handle it. This would have thinned their numbers, requiring them to become even more involved.
Somebody like Aetheris would have activated his true form, rising to 12 meters, if not higher, now that his True Name and bloodline had awakened.
That, of course, would have rendered not only their Plan A obsolete but also the subsequent plans down to D, meaning they would have been forced to use their Gradeless skills and true forms.

In a way, facing those realms above them had proven to be more complex than they expected. Facing a Spirit King and Emperor in a one-on-one battle would be easy, but the moment they came in hordes, they would have to adapt, and that meant abandoning their plans.
Kent realized that, and it brought a smile to his face.

Their determination to grow beyond their current limits and even face hordes of beasts, several realms above them, without having to expend too much of their strength was evident, and he knew what had to be done.
"I think you guys are mistaken about something. This is a medium world, and so far, only a few in this world can measure up to you. Basically, you are invincible in medium worlds.
So, instead of looking defeated, take pride in knowing that you went after a horde of bloodthirsty tigers and came out unscathed.
I mean, how many in the medium worlds can brag about the same thing? You are basically invincible here, so don’t think too much about this minor setback.
However, since you all think you haven’t reached your combat limits, then I will take you to a place where you can see if there is more you can do to raise your limit beyond what it already is."
Hearing Kent’s words and plan seemed to lift their spirits a bit.
"Master, where are you taking us?" Kaizo asked, his usual smile returning to his face.
"Fedora. It is a high world, and while it isn’t the strongest, it currently has more than enough troubles that, with your presence, can be solved.
You will spend one-month training with the best of their warriors, and when you think you’ve had enough, you can lead operations to destabilize the Orc Alliance further.
In all, for the next three months, you will stay there and train to your limit before getting back to the Dungeon."
Kent’s plan is simple. Fedora is a high world, so he plans on making them face those many odds and see if they can handle the pressure.
If they manage to transcend their weaknesses, they will be able to better implement their plans in the coming battles inside the Dungeon.
"Prepare. We leave in an hour."
Kent vanished and appeared inside the mountain garden. He planned on spending a few minutes with the three lolis before going back out there.
However, Kent was greeted with the shock of his life.
"They are asleep." Kent stood stunned, watching the three lolis hugging each other as they slept, looking relatively peaceful.

"Do they even sleep?" The shock was plain. As far as he knew, the three sisters weren’t capable of falling asleep. If anything, they were always up to doing one annoying thing after another. So this was a shock to him.
However, they were asleep now, and that told him all he needed to know.
"Something that I am not aware of happened to them. The fact that all three of them were sleeping at the same time said it all. Something is wrong."
He walked closer and felt their temperature; however, they looked and felt fine. This further made Kent think that something had happened to them.
"Was this my fault? The last time something happened to them was when I nearly lost myself, and Dori had to strain herself to save me.
But I didn’t lose my mind this time. Even if I did, it should be only Dori sleeping right now. But for all three of them to... Tower, what happened?"
⟦Nothing I can explain. However, from my scan, they appear to be fine, so the master shouldn’t worry. I will keep a close eye on them, and if anything changes, I will ensure you are informed.⟧
"Okay." Kent looked at the three lolis again before vanishing back to the harem tower. Now, there were three more people he had to worry about.
When he appeared in the harem tower, the sisters were all in the glasshouse except Alina, who was still in the grid space.
Kent had to handle her, too, so he entered her grid space, as he had admin access. Alina gave him complete access to the grid space, just as all his wives had given him access.
Despite Alina wanting to remain isolated, even temporarily revoking her sisters’ access to her space, the one person she didn’t have the heart to block from entering was Kent.
So Kent entered, and what he saw left his jaw hanging.

chapters.title: Chapter 794: Back To Fedora
paragraphs: Perhaps Kent expected to find a broken, weeping, and sad Alina upon entering her Grid Space. Of course, anyone would have expected the same thing.
After all, when she went back to her grid space, she was weeping.
However, what greeted Kent was anything but a sad Alina. When he entered her Grid Space, he found Alina hard at work.
In the air were thousands, perhaps millions, of runes glowing in different shades of color. She was also actively drawing runes, showing no sign of stopping at any moment.
And since inside her Grid Space, she didn’t need to use her energy to hold the runes, she could draw billions before using them to create the arrays and formations.
So Kent just stood there staring at her as she continued to draw for twenty good minutes before he finally cleared his throat.
That was when Alina realized Kent was inside her space, causing her to stop. She looked at him for a few moments before bowing her head, planting her gaze on the ground.
"You look funny," Kent said, walking toward her. Soon, he was standing in front of her. Then he reached out and hugged her.
Alina immediately started crying in his arms.
Not that Kent minded, for he knew to some extent Alina saw herself as inferior when in fact she was the most dangerous of them all.
But who could blame her for thinking that?
All of her sisters were warriors with their weapons, while she just had to be guarded before she could analyze a battlefield and draw the correct formation or array to handle it.
Of course, long before Kent awakened her True Name, she never knew what she could bring to the harem aside from the fact that her man was obsessed with her butt.
She always thinks of her rule, what she would do when her man’s life is in danger. She knew using her butt to save him was not an option. So she never knew she would become this impressive.
But that she did.
Now that she has awakened this incredible skill and talent, instead of utilizing it effectively, she is now failing her team, a team that relies on her to ensure their first plans always succeed.
To someone like her, who had felt inferior for a long time, being the heart of her team was the greatest honor she had ever received.
They trusted her always to come through when she was needed the most. However, this time around, she failed to meet expectations.
That broke her heart.
"Stop crying, Alina. None of what happened was your fault. Not one of your sisters died, nor did any of your friends, so take the win.
Though I must say, you and your sisters are being petty. In the end, you won the battle, so why are you sour? Lighten up and take solace in knowing you won in the end.
A day will come when all five plans will fail. When that day comes and you fail to meet their expectations, then you can be this sour and weepy. For now, know that it was a setback, not a failure."
Kent lifted her head and planted a kiss on her forehead.

Alina took a few minutes to stop crying before looking at the runes in the air. After a few seconds, she looked back at Kent, and a slight smile—one that didn’t quite reach her eyes—appeared on her face, showing it was half sincere, half fake.
She wanted to cheer Kent up and assure him she was fine. But Kent knew her better than she did, so he pulled her closer, and as expected, his hands found her butt and started kneading it.

"Don’t see yourself as a failure, Alina. You are my wife, and every last one of my wives is no failure. When you should have given up after your mother died, you didn’t; instead, you chose to live on, and now you are here.
That alone tells you what you are. You are a warrior just like every last one of your sisters.
So live like one, for there will be many setbacks and failures in the future, and if you let them kill your spirit, then your future as a true warrior might as well be shattered now."
Alina nodded, a subtle moan escaping her lips as she looked at the smug look on Kent’s face.
"You always know the right words to say and what to do."
"That’s because I am awesome." Kent raised her into his arms, making Alina wrap her legs around his waist. Kent, of course, shamelessly sank his fingers into her soft ass, causing Alina to giggle.
Just like that, she had recovered somehow.
"So what are you aiming for, drawing hundreds of thousands in less than a day?" Kent asked, now that Alina was in a good mood and right mind to talk.
"It is a project that will one day shake battlefields. I call it the Battlefield Matrix. Sometimes, you need setbacks to realize what has to be done."
"How does it work, and when will you complete it?"

"The Battlefield Matrix will be a grid that, when opened on battlefields, will act like Divine Sense. It will spread across the battlefield and actively monitor situations, including both hidden and emerging threats.
It will understand the flow of the battle and connect with my mind, allowing me to adapt and determine the best array or formation to deploy.
Of course, that will be the start. As time passes, I can add millions of attacking and defending arrays to it, which will activate based on the nature of the battle and when new situations arise.

As to when it will be done, it can be 100 years from now, 1,000, or perhaps a million years. However, I can start using it from my next battle. Though it will be the basic form of it, as my current understanding of runes is still limited."
"I guess you have things figured out in the end. I am proud of you," Kent said, but inwardly, he was wondering whether Alina truly understood what she was doing.
’If this were Earth, I would say she was aiming to create an Artificial Intelligence model aimed at analyzing battles, adapting, and acting based on the situation on the battlefield.
Good thing I know a thing or two about Artificial Intelligence.’ Kent smiled, looking at the proud look on Alina’s face.

’Since this is what you wanted to do, I will make sure your dreams come true. Also, this is my time to nerd up and make sure that when all is said and done, the battlefield will tremble at your presence.’
Kent didn’t know where this reasoning of hers came from. It was all too modern and mundane.

But he understood one thing: if what she said was indeed what she aimed for, then there was a chance that she would become something akin to a Sovereign of the Matrix, someone whose presence encompasses all battlefields and nothing, no matter how minute it is, will escape her sight.

’I hope you succeed, Alina, I really do, for this will be very difficult to create, but if you manage to break free of all limitations, you will become someone who wouldn’t make mistakes when in combat.’
Kent walked out of the grid space with Alina in his arms. When he arrived in the harem tower, he could sense the jealous looks from her sisters, especially when they saw what his hands were doing.
He just laughed, and soon, he was in Fedora with everyone except Vexthra and Camilla.

You are my wife, and every last one of my wives is no failure.
When you should have given up after your mother died, you didn’t; instead, you chose to live on, and now you are here.
That alone tells you what you are.
You are a warrior just like every last one of your sisters.
So live like one, for there will be many setbacks and failures in the future, and if you let them kill your spirit, then your future as a true warrior might as well be shattered now."
Alina nodded, a subtle moan escaping her lips as she looked at the smug look on Kent’s face.
"You always know the right words to say and what to do."
"That’s because I am awesome." Kent raised her into his arms, making Alina wrap her legs around his waist.
Kent, of course, shamelessly sank his fingers into her soft ass, causing Alina to giggle.
Just like that, she had recovered somehow.
"So what are you aiming for, drawing hundreds of thousands in less than a day?" Kent asked, now that Alina was in a good mood and right mind to talk.
"It is a project that will one day shake battlefields.
I call it the Battlefield Matrix.
Sometimes, you need setbacks to realize what has to be done."
"How does it work, and when will you complete it?"
"The Battlefield Matrix will be a grid that, when opened on battlefields, will act like Divine Sense.
It will spread across the battlefield and actively monitor situations, including both hidden and emerging threats.
It will understand the flow of the battle and connect with my mind, allowing me to adapt and determine the best array or formation to deploy.
Of course, that will be the start.
As time passes, I can add millions of attacking and defending arrays to it, which will activate based on the nature of the battle and when new situations arise.
As to when it will be done, it can be 100 years from now, 1,000, or perhaps a million years.
However, I can start using it from my next battle.
Though it will be the basic form of it, as my current understanding of runes is still limited."
"I guess you have things figured out in the end.
I am proud of you," Kent said, but inwardly, he was wondering whether Alina truly understood what she was doing.
’If this were Earth, I would say she was aiming to create an Artificial Intelligence model aimed at analyzing battles, adapting, and acting based on the situation on the battlefield.
Good thing I know a thing or two about Artificial Intelligence.’ Kent smiled, looking at the proud look on Alina’s face.
’Since this is what you wanted to do, I will make sure your dreams come true.
Also, this is my time to nerd up and make sure that when all is said and done, the battlefield will tremble at your presence.’
Kent didn’t know where this reasoning of hers came from.
It was all too modern and mundane.

But he understood one thing: if what she said was indeed what she aimed for, then there was a chance that she would become something akin to a Sovereign of the Matrix, someone whose presence encompasses all battlefields and nothing, no matter how minute it is, will escape her sight.

’I hope you succeed, Alina, I really do, for this will be very difficult to create, but if you manage to break free of all limitations, you will become someone who wouldn’t make mistakes when in combat.’
Kent walked out of the grid space with Alina in his arms.
When he arrived in the harem tower, he could sense the jealous looks from her sisters, especially when they saw what his hands were doing.
He just laughed, and soon, he was in Fedora with everyone except Vexthra and Camilla.

chapters.title: Chapter 795: Timeline shift [Bonus]
paragraphs: "Welcome back to Emberwood, Kent," King Hkum said, shaking Kent’s hand the moment he and his team arrived in Emberwood.
Since Kent had been there before, he could now open the portal there at will without even the need to use the World Teleporter.
Of course, even without that, he could teleport there since he is their Guardian now. Being a guardian came with so many perks.
"It’s good to be back, King Hkum," Kent responded, a smile playing on his lips. He could sense it; the king had become much stronger than the last time he was there.
"How is everyone?" Kent asked, noticing only the king around to welcome him.

"The Queen and the Princesses went to have some discussions with some of our allies. They will be back in a few days. As for the elders, they have gone to investigate a sudden rumour spreading through the orc alliance."
"Oh, a rumor," Kent raised his brow. He could already sense a conspiracy brewing on the horizon, and if what his instincts told him was true, then his legion would have so much fun here.
"Let’s talk inside," the king proposed, and Kent nodded. He would want to know what was happening and make sure his legion settled in before leaving.
Soon, they were inside the throne room. Of course, his legion had already started roaming the city, for they’d been there before, and they were familiar with some of the Foxkins.
He settled down, and the king began to speak.

"About three weeks ago, rumors started spreading that a Pill Monarch had appeared in the land of the Orcs. According to the report, or rather, a rumor, the Pill Monarch is at the Heavenly Ascension stage and seems to have some connection with King Balma.
We don’t know if the reports are accurate, but a Pill Monarch coming from another world to ours isn’t something we can doubt, so I deployed the elders to go investigate.
If the reports are indeed accurate, then we will be facing much bigger odds than we already have on our hands."
Kent nodded at the king’s words. If the rumors were indeed true, then the danger they’d be facing would be too much to handle.

Right now, Kent knew he couldn’t handle a Spirit Lord. Of course, Val could use her cheat to handle one. But even so, when it comes to Heavenly Ascension stage warriors, that becomes a different thing altogether.
Even in her Moon Goddess form, with her limited cultivation base, she would struggle, and at any moment, she might even lose.
So the danger is indeed severe on this front, and Kent could sense it.
Of course, aside from the fact that there is a potential Heavenly Ascension stage warrior on the side of the enemy, this one is also an alchemist.
Aside from his perhaps overpowered flame arts, he is a Pill Monarch, which means the time for the poison to be manually handled by the Orc king has been reduced.
Now, Kent can already see the bastard recovering in less than a year with the Pill Monarch’s help.
This means the moment he has recovered, he will come after the rebel alliance, and that will be catastrophic when King Hkum still hasn’t reached the peak of the Spirit Lord stage.
Aside from that, the other leaders of the Rebel Alliance are still sitting at the peak of the Spirit Sovereign stage.
This holds a clear indication that the endgame will be bad for them, and Kent can already see that happening.
"This is indeed bad." Kent rubbed his hand and asked, "What about the Hellhounds and the Lions? Are they still fighting?"

"They stopped. However, they are still hostile toward each other, so the chances of them being a true team in the Orc Alliance will be slim. However, they don’t have to be a team to fight for the same cause.
However, thanks to their battle, their numbers have thinned down, so the threat that will come from there will be limited."
"Good. I guess the plan worked better than I anticipated. Of course, the Orc Alliance remains stronger because it has the Orc King at its helm.
However, with the Lionkin and Hellhounds fractured, we can pick them apart. And I think I have the perfect team for it.
My team is currently going through a phase after their recent defeat, so they need a cause to reignite their battle spirit. That was why I brought them here.

For the next few weeks, they will train with the finest of your warriors. When they come to terms with their resolve, they will spend two more months here, going on a series of missions to further destabilize the ranks of the Hellhounds and the Lionkin.
That said, we have about a year before the Orc King recovers, so we have to start planning for it now. I will do what I can on my end to secure ways to handle whatever odds they may throw at us.
However, until then, use the next few months to find as many treasures from the list I provided and try to upgrade at least two of each of the Battle Dolls I gave you.
If you manage to get them to the level of a Spirit Emperor, that will play a massive role in the endgame. For now, continue to raise your strength level...
I will leave additional resources for you and your allies to utilize, further strengthening your ranks."
King Hkum nodded at Kent’s words. "Thank you, Kent. Without you, by now, the Orcs would have long destroyed us."
"Don’t worry about it. I am the guardian of this race, so I have to protect everyone at all costs."
Kent went on to discuss a few things with the king. Later, he left to discuss the plans with his legion about their activities in Fedora.
Afterward, he checked up on Sword King Shawn, who, if things go well, will be able to bridge the gap in strength and give the rebel alliance a shot at winning.
He was currently at a stage where his foundation, as Dori described, had regressed to its basic level, and he was rebuilding it.
Once all that was done, not only would his foundation become unshakable, but he would also gain a better understanding of his sword path and be able to improve his sword realm.
The plan was rather simple. All he had to do was utilize his superior understanding of the sword to enhance his sword foundation, starting from the basics.
He was on that path and would soon become undisputed in the way of the sword.
The next few hours were spent giving the king all kinds of resources they would need to build their strength and even share with their allies.
In a way, their allies would believe them more, which Kent estimated would trigger the [Guardian Allies] and add more soul essence to his stockpile.
He also selected five warriors and added them to the [Guardian Hand]. They were given their own resources, and soon, Kent knew he would start seeing significant improvements from them.
If he wanted to bridge the gap between him and the Spirit Lords, then he must build his soul universe, making it much more potent for when he truly needs it.
When all that was done, he left and headed back to the tower to handle his own business. He had five days outside and 120 days in the tower. That’s a long time to accomplish a great deal.

chapters.title: Chapter 796: Reporting to the Elders [Bonus]
paragraphs: [Supreme Immortal Sect - Grand Hall: Outer Region]
The location of the Supreme Immortal Sect, to this day, remains unknown to all except those who have been admitted to the sect as disciples.

Only disciples and elders are privileged to know the location of the sect. Of course, in a way that nobody can describe, even those who know the location tend to forget it whenever they are away from the sect.
But they will always be able to find their way back, regardless of how forgetful they are. Even so, unless they want you to come with them, you won’t be able to follow them. It is a bizarre place.
So, while those who even fail to pass the entrance can be likened to knowing the location, the moment they are out of the sect, all that memory of the sect’s actual location becomes scrambled.
However, that is to be expected, as the Supreme Immortal Sect is located in a world before the fall, where the laws are more visible and the limitations on the medium world are more lax.
Although the strongest being is still at the Core Formation stage, due to the relaxed nature of the limitations, their growth speed is high.
There are people there who are currently at the Core Formation stage, but they hold so much power that they can rival even Spirit Emperors in an average High world.
When the Battle of Parting occurred, the entire world was in turmoil, and many things were destroyed; however, not the sect, which had stood for millions of years.
It was the largest sect back when there was no limit on the world, and people could reach the peak of the Heavenly Ascension in this world before ascending to an immortal world.
Its heritage spans several years, and because of its rich history and resources, it manages to hold Sonox as the third strongest world in the Celestial Conclave planetary alliance.
This makes them one of the top three sects within fifty worlds.
Elder Lance came to the sect with dreams of making it big, and while he was the strongest in his world thanks to the sect, he was merely an outer elder of the Supreme Immortal Sect.
To get back from Sonox to the sect, one would have to cross the Humming Void, an ancient battlefield of two powerful cultivators.
It is a perilous place that requires careful navigation. So, while he and the two disciples left right after the tower closed, it took them a day and a half to return to the sect.
Upon getting back, Elder Lance ran to the hall to report his shocking discovery.
Inside a grand hall, five people, each powerful in their own right, were having a discussion.
"I heard this year that the number of disciples required for the interplanetary competition will be twenty, and five seeded candidates for us.
That will be five more than one hundred years ago. Is the alliance perhaps trying to add more bloody challenges to the competition?" Supreme Elder Jian said, causing the elders to nod.
"There will be more deaths than the last time, and knowing the history between us and the Primal Beast Sect, there will be fierce competition.
We better prepare our disciples well, and perhaps this time out, the loss will be minimal," Elder Aster, a beautiful, dark-haired elf, said.

"At least we have the Pill Princess, the Ice Maiden, that one-eyed demon spawn, the Venom King, and that Arrogant Crystal Dragon Prince. With them leading, I am sure we will come out on top, even beating the Celestial Gate Sect."
"You make it sound like the top-ranked sect for the past eighty thousand years are weaklings, like those useless beings in Sonox.

Unlike them, the Celestial Gate world is a powerful world filled with monsters. They are the leaders of the alliance, and they have many connections to High worlds and even Immortal worlds. They aren’t at all weak," Elder Xior added, looking smug as if he were better than everyone there.
However, there is some truth to what he said.

Unlike the Supreme Immortal Sect, which has most of its disciples from other worlds, the Celestial Gate sect takes its disciples, or at least the majority of them, from the Celestial Gate world, so they are several times stronger than Sonox.
"Even so, we have some of the geniuses the sect has never seen in thousands of years joining the competition, and they will even be added as seeded candidates for the main competition.
We are not weak in any—"
BANG!
Suddenly, the door to the hall was swung open, and Elder Lance ran in like he was being chased.
"Who dares enter without permission?" Supreme Elder Jian released his aura, freezing Elder Lance in his tracks.
He turned pale immediately, not even having the strength to utter a word.
Thankfully, Supreme Elder Jian released him in the next couple of seconds, realizing he was the one he told to go conduct the Flame Tower Trial.
"Speak."
Elder Lance shuddered but recovered quickly and started to speak.
"I carried out this year’s Flame Tower Trial in Sonox and will now be giving my report."

"Tch, those useless beings still dare think they can make it here by learning a few flame arts. They will come and see if they can pass even the first exams we have prepared this year," Elder Xior chuckled, his voice dripping with arrogance.
Perhaps after spending thousands of years in the sect, he had forgotten his lineage.
"Go ahead," Elder Jian cast a glance at the flame demon and gestured for Elder Lance to continue... Elder Lance smirked inwardly, knowing this smug elder was about to get the shock of his life.

"Among the hundreds that entered, 60 qualified to take the entrance exams. Among them, 20 managed to learn Heaven grade flame arts, 10 managed to learn Legendary grade flame arts, and six managed to learn Mystical grade flame arts."
"I count 36, Elder Lance. Are you perhaps losing your touch when it comes to counting?" Supreme Elder Jian asked, and Elder Lance smiled.
"No, Supreme Elder, I can count perfectly. You see, while Sonox was said to be a trash world, I beg to differ, for what I saw and experienced is far more than I expected from such a place.

Among the 57, 24 made it to level four, some even learning multiple Mythic grade flame arts—something the Pill Princess was able to learn just two. Some managed to learn four others, seven, and the highest learned eight Mythic grade flame arts."
"WHAT?"
All the elders were taken aback, their faces displaying shocked expressions.
"That is not all. Out of the 24 that reached the fourth level, 12 advanced to the fifth level, with 11 managing to learn one Divine-grade flame art and the top ranker learning 12 Divine-grade arts.
If you don’t believe me, then see a captured recording of the display board, and you will see I am not lying."
Elder Lance activated the video he had captured of the recording, and even at the end, he purposely included Kent in the recording to make a point.
"What is a human doing there? I thought they regressed after the Wynthralls ascended," Elder Kenna, an orc-human, asked, looking at the handsome Kent who appeared in the video.
"I don’t think your intel is correct, Elder Kenna. The top ranker is this human. His name is Kent Madson, and he was the one who learned 12 Divine-grade flame arts.
And guess what, he learned all 12 in under an hour, completely mastering all forms of it."
With a smug smile, Elder Lance ended his report, giving the elders time to ponder what they’d just heard and seen.

chapters.title: Chapter 797: Everything Is Automated
paragraphs: [Inside the Tower - 120 days seclusion; Day 1]
After handling everything, Kent settled down in the sword tower to attend to his primary objectives for entering this short seclusion.
The first thing he wanted to learn was how to create Flame Veins and Flame Cores. Of course, he already has a manual for both processes.
"Agni said it will take time to start forming the veins, that I will need powerful flame essence to be able to manage it.
So I guess I’d better learn the method now, and the rest will be handled after I get to the sect." Kent took out the scroll for creating flame veins and unfurled it.

"Wow, that is one complex diagram," Kent smiled, looking at the intricate design. The diagram is the structure that governs how the body functions, how energy is channeled, and how flame veins can be created.
Essentially, he was about to alter the structure of his body, adding more organs, which, in this case, would significantly enhance his power in all aspects.

It’s like genetic modification, only this time, instead of modifying his body using DNA from other beings, he would be creating new organs—108,000 of them, to be exact—and he would have to do all that while inside the hottest flame region he could find.
"According to Agni, it took him 300 years to fully learn this complex method. However, since I am a genius, this shouldn’t take too long."
Kent smiled and then made the unfurled scroll hover in the air before him.
He channeled his energy into it, and before he could even blink, his consciousness was pulled into the technique.
He appeared within a realm of flames, where everything was made of fire. The stones, plants, rivers, and even the very ground he stood on were made from lava.
However, the sky was not made of flame; instead, it was composed of millions of miniature diagrams formed from runes.
There were just millions of them, and looking past them, Kent could see a large door hidden in the clouds.
"That’s a lot of diagrams. No wonder it took a genius like Agni 300 years to learn this technique," Kent scratched the back of his head.
"Per his teaching, I need to learn and understand every diagram. Every success creates a step that will lead me to the gate of Flame Evolution hidden in the cloud.
The moment I open that door, I can begin walking the path of Flame Vein Creation."
Kent sighed and then sat down. He had a lot of work to do and little time to complete it. He closed his eyes and formed a seal.
The moment the seal formed, a diagram moved and slowly entered his forehead. Kent felt a small understanding of the flame enter his mind.
He quickly began channeling more diagrams into his mind. Soon, he was being bombarded by thousands of diagrams every minute.
A day quickly went by, but the number of diagrams left to learn still numbered in the millions; however, the speed at which Kent was learning them was much faster than one would expect.
After two days, the number started to show signs of reduction. By this time, Kent had learned over a million diagrams.
Three days later, it became apparent that he was learning more and more diagrams as the number of runes started to dwindle.
The process was complex, and although he was making progress, as the days passed, his speed began to slow down.
Of course, sometimes it hastened, and at other times it slowed down.
However, as more and more diagrams entered his mind, a stairway began to form toward the door in the clouds.
[Day 25 into mastering the Flame Vein Creation Art]
Kent’s body on the outside started showing signs of change. At first, his soul flame surged and burned his shirt. However, as the days passed, changes began to appear on his body.
On the 25th day, as he was diligently studying the manual, a flame tattoo appeared on Kent’s chest, pulsating with energy.

At first, it was just a tattoo, but as time passed, the tattoo began to spread all over his skin, almost as if it had a life of its own. On the 30th day, it moved and stopped when it reached his forehead.
That was when the true progress Kent never expected started to happen.
Inside the technique space, the diagrams began entering his mind much faster the moment the tattoo stopped at his forehead.

By the 50th day, only a few diagrams remained. By the time the 50th day came to a close, the last diagram moved and entered his forehead, and the final step leading to the door formed, stopping in front of the door.
Kent opened his eyes and stood up.
"That took longer than I anticipated, but I am not there yet." He stepped on the first step, and soon, he was on his way toward the door.
If Agni or anyone who had ever learned this technique heard Kent saying it took him more time than it should, they would probably pull on his ear and spank him for his shameless and rude comment.
A genius like Agni had to spend 300 years learning it, and Kent was already complaining after spending just 50 days.
The audacity of his words said it all.
Soon, he was in front of the door, and with a gentle push, the door opened, and his eyes opened on the inside.
Messages quickly appeared before his eyes.
⟦Congratulations on successfully learning the Flame Vein Creation Manual⟧
⟦Your Primordial Infinity Dragon Art has activated⟧
Kent felt a rush of energy wash through his body, then a new message appeared.
⟦Your Primordial Infinity Dragon Art is merging with the Flame Vein Creation Manual⟧
⟦Merging was successful⟧
⟦Congratulations, your cultivation technique grade has been upgraded from Celestial ↠ Primordial⟧
Kent raised his brow, reading the message.
"Looks like I did something good again." He smiled and then checked the last message, bringing an even bigger smile to his face.
⟦The Flame Vein Creation Manual has merged with your cultivation technique. Whenever you are close to a flame source, the flame vein creation process will automatically start⟧
"Everything is automated," Kent smiled, feeling like he had just won the lottery.

The process that requires one to meticulously stay in a flame-rich region, using hundreds, perhaps thousands, of years to form flame veins, can now be achieved by merely walking through flame-rich regions.
"At this rate, I will just pack my bag and go stay in the Flame Valley for a while. I am sure by the time I leave there, I will form a couple of flame veins."
Kent channeled his energy through his body to see if there were any changes.
He indeed sensed something had changed about his body. Now, he felt that his body lacked considerable strength.
At first, he could feel that his body was perfectly adjusted. But now, he could tell he was missing some things. These things, of course, were the flame veins he had yet to form.
"The sect better have a flame-rich training area, else I will be pissed."
⟦Congratulations to the master for mastering the Flame Vein Creation Manual. The next on your schedule is the Flame Core Creation Manual⟧.
"Thanks, Tower, but when did you create a schedule for me?" Kent asked with a smirk.
⟦As the master grows, so do I, and at this moment in my growth, I saw it best to create a schedule for the master, emphasizing the essential tasks so the master wouldn’t forget⟧
"That is thoughtful of you, Tower. Then I guess I will start learning the second manual now."

chapters.title: Chapter 798: Grand Pyris Pill Pagoda
paragraphs: ⟦The Flame Core Creation Manual has merged with your cultivation technique. Whenever you are close to a flame source, the flame core creation process will automatically start.
However, the core creation process will begin only after you create your first 25,000 flame veins.⟧
The second manual was mastered in ten days.
It followed the same structure as the Flame Vein Creation Manual, and since Kent had already been through the process, it became relatively simple for him to master.
However, the moment he was done, the message he received was clear and similar to what Agni told him: without the Flame Veins, he wouldn’t be able to form Flame Cores.
"Now, I just need to create the veins, and everything will take care of itself." Kent stood up and headed to the Alchemy Tower to do something he had been hoping to try all this time.

When he awakened the Alchemy Tower, he received some items that, when used the right way, would further aid his understanding of pill making. Inside the harem tower, he had the love garden, the yin pool, and the like.
Inside the Alchemy Tower, there is a Pill World room where, upon entering, he will be transported into a dreamlike state to witness alchemy from a different perspective.
He has a similar feature in his sword tower and has been trying to make good use of it for a while, but hasn’t yet.

Now, he planned on using the Pill World to kill time and perhaps learn something new about alchemy before going to the sect where he would be facing someone so far that he had heard only fantastic things about.
So he entered the Pill World room inside the Alchemy Tower, where a game-like pod was set at the center of the room.
"Tower, wake me up when the time to go to the sect is nearing," Kent gave an order to the tower before sleeping in the pod.
The moment he entered, his vision turned hazy, and then he was pulled into a realm beyond his own.
[Planet Pyris – Grand Pill Pagoda: 7th Floor (340,7000 years ago)]
Kent appeared in a large hall filled with people of different races.
The first thing he noticed was the distinct color of the clothes most people were wearing, regardless of their race.

The majority were clad in green robes and cloaks of different designs. Most had emblems on them that indicated the sect to which they belonged. A few also wore distinctive clothes that showed their family’s origin.
Naturally, all these people were the alchemists in the world he had been pulled into.
He examined his surroundings, taking in races such as demons, elves, humans, dragons, elementals, and many more, all found in the same world.
This means the world he was pulled into is a much bigger one, housing more than 20 different races that he could count.
"Brother, you look like you’re lost." Suddenly, a young elf tapped Kent on the shoulder, prompting him to turn around.
When his gaze landed on the young elf clad in a green robe of the Lotus Bloom Pill Sect, his brow furrowed.
’He can see me,’ Kent thought inwardly.

’Was Gaia messing with me by telling me nobody would see me when in the Pill World?’ Kent’s mind was a mix of shock and intrigue. He never expected to be seen. But now that he was seen, a whole different door opened for him.
"Yes, brother..."
"Suoh."
"Yes, brother Suoh, I am indeed lost." Kent smiled. "This happens to be my first time here, so I am a little lost."
"I get it, brother..."
"Kent"
"It happens to the best of us. I was lost when I first came here, and it took me some time to figure things out, but eventually, I did.
However, don’t worry, I will help you understand all you want to know about this place," Suoh said with a rather happy smile.
"Thank you, brother Suoh. I will be rather happy to learn more about this place."
The handsome elf smiled. "But of course. For someone of your status to be allowed here on the 7th floor, you must be from one of the 5 Pill Families.
As such, it is my duty to help you to the best of my abilities. Just don’t forget, my name is Suoh."
Hearing his words, Kent turned and looked at his chest. That was when he saw the Pill Grandmaster badge hanging there.
It was then that everything clicked.
’I guess as a Pill Grandmaster, I had no business being on this floor. But he thinks I am from an influential family, and that was why I was allowed access.
So, he is doing this to curry favor with my supposed family when, in fact, I am not from any influential family. But I can use this to my advantage.’
"I will be sure to remember your name, brother Suoh." Hearing Kent’s words, the handsome elf smiled.
"Welcome to the Grand Pyris Pill Pagoda. This is the 7th floor, where only alchemists from the Pill Sage stage are allowed access. I am a Pill Sage with a silver badge.

I don’t know if you’re aware, but having a silver badge is a significant achievement in the grand scheme of things when considering Pill Sages. Of course, soon, I will get my gold and platinum badge, and then I can upgrade to become a Pill King."
Talk about selling oneself for opportunity—Suoh was indeed doing a terrific job at that. Kent could only smile, knowing none of this would go anywhere.
Suoh thought Kent was from a renewed family, but Kent knew that in fact, he was from nowhere. But he chose to play Suoh’s game.
"I am sure Brother Suoh has the talent to rise to the peak. I really think so," Kent smiled, seeing the pleased expression in Suoh’s eyes.
"By the way, why don’t we start from the basics first, like, is this a medium, high, or immortal world?" Kent asked.

"Pyris is a high world. It is one of the ten Pill Worlds on this side of the galaxy. Of course, with your background, you already know a Pill world is one of the most powerful worlds in many star systems in the high worlds.

Pyris is ranked 7th and is one of the hubs for alchemists. The place we are in right now is the Grand Pyris Pill Pagoda, a 12-floor pagoda where the greatest knowledge one needs on the path of alchemy can be found.

We are currently, as I said earlier, on the 7th floor. And today, there will be a duel between two Pill Kings. I don’t know if you know them, but they are two of the best Pill Kings in the Pyris Pill Alliance.
The fact that you are here should be a blessing for you, as you will witness some impeccable flame control techniques that only a few are privileged to study.
I heard there is a secret chamber in the pagoda where those who are privileged to enter will come into contact with a piece of the Grand Pill Tablet, a relic left by the first Pill Celestial."

Kent’s heart shook when he heard the Grand Pill Tablet. The word sounded familiar to him, and that suddenly ignited his hunger to see this tablet or the piece of it currently hidden inside the Grand Pyris Pill Pagoda.

"Do you happen to know the name of this Pill Celestial?" Kent asked, hungry to know more; however, before Suoh could answer him, a Pill Emperor entered the large hall, causing everyone to quiet down immediately.
